**[Section 15 --- FINMA Regulatory Requirements]{.underline}**

**[15.1 --- Close-Out Netting Opinions]{.underline}**

Prior to executing any GMRA, Legal must confirm that a current (within 12 months) enforceability opinion on close-out netting under the laws of the counterparty\'s jurisdiction is on file. The opinion must be provided by a law firm approved by Voss Bank\'s Chief Legal Officer and must cover the following matters:

> • The enforceability of the GMRA\'s close-out netting provisions (Paragraph 10) under the laws of the counterparty\'s jurisdiction of organisation.
>
> • The enforceability of close-out netting in the event of the counterparty\'s insolvency, including any applicable insolvency safe harbours or exemptions.
>
> • For US counterparties, the opinion must specifically address SIPA/SIPC treatment of repo collateral and the enforceability of netting under the US Bankruptcy Code safe harbours (11 U.S.C. §§ 559, 561, and related provisions). The opinion must confirm that repo transactions under the GMRA qualify as \"repurchase agreements\" for the purposes of the Bankruptcy Code safe harbours and that the Non-Defaulting Party\'s contractual right to liquidate, terminate, or accelerate is protected from the automatic stay.

The netting opinion must be refreshed at least annually (i.e., a new opinion must be obtained within 12 months of the date of the most recent opinion). If a netting opinion is more than 12 months old at the time of execution of a new GMRA or at the time of entry into a new Transaction under an existing GMRA, the desk must not proceed until a refreshed opinion is obtained.

Legal maintains a register of all netting opinions on file, including the jurisdiction, the date of the opinion, the opining law firm, and the expiry date. The desk should check this register before commencing any new GMRA negotiation.

**[15.2 --- Capital Treatment]{.underline}**

The GMRA must include terms sufficient to ensure that reverse repo transactions qualify for securities financing transaction (SFT) treatment under the Basel III framework as implemented by FINMA (Capital Adequacy Ordinance (CAO), Art. 56 et seq.). SFT treatment allows Voss Bank to recognise the collateral received under reverse repo transactions for the purposes of calculating credit risk-weighted assets and leverage ratio exposure, subject to compliance with the applicable eligibility conditions.

Key conditions for SFT treatment include:

> • The GMRA must provide for enforceable close-out netting (see Section 15.1).
>
> • The collateral must be revalued at least daily (which is ensured by the GMRA\'s standard margin maintenance provisions).
>
> • The collateral must be liquid and must not exhibit a material positive correlation with the credit quality of the counterparty (this is ensured by the Eligible Collateral criteria set out in Section 3).

Haircuts below HQLA floors (see Section 3.3) may cause the transaction to attract higher capital charges under the standardised approach supervisory haircut framework. If haircuts approach the HQLA floors, the desk must escalate to Treasury (Zürich) to confirm the capital impact before agreeing the haircut level.

**[15.3 --- Large Exposure Reporting]{.underline}**

Aggregate gross exposure to a single counterparty under the GMRA must be monitored against FINMA large exposure limits. Under the FINMA framework, a bank\'s total exposure to a single counterparty (or group of connected counterparties) may not exceed 25% of the bank\'s eligible capital (Tier 1 capital plus Tier 2 capital, subject to applicable limits).

The Net Exposure Cap set by the Credit Committee for each counterparty is designed to remain well within the FINMA large exposure limit, providing a buffer against fluctuations in exposure due to market movements, new trades, or collateral value changes. The desk should be aware that the Net Exposure Cap is not the same as the large exposure limit --- the Cap is typically set at a level significantly below the regulatory limit to allow headroom for operational and market-driven exposure increases.

If the aggregate gross exposure to a counterparty under the GMRA approaches the Net Exposure Cap, or if the desk becomes aware of circumstances that could cause the aggregate exposure to exceed the FINMA large exposure limit (including exposure under other master agreements, such as the ISDA Master Agreement), the desk must immediately notify Risk Management (Zürich) and the Credit Committee.

**[Section 16 --- Non-Commercial Drafting Mark-Ups]{.underline}**

**[16.1 --- General Approach]{.underline}**

In any GMRA negotiation, the counterparty\'s counsel will typically propose a number of non-commercial drafting mark-ups in addition to the substantive commercial and legal proposals addressed in the preceding sections. Non-commercial mark-ups include, without limitation:

> • Clarifications to defined terms that do not alter commercial substance.
>
> • Conforming changes to ensure internal consistency within the GMRA and Annex I.
>
> • Typographical corrections.
>
> • Notice mechanic refinements (e.g., updating notice addresses, adding email as a permitted notice method, adjusting deemed-receipt provisions).
>
> • Cross-referencing corrections.
>
> • Grammatical and stylistic changes.

These non-commercial mark-ups should be assessed on their merits. While they do not typically raise commercial or risk concerns, they may inadvertently alter the legal effect of a provision if not reviewed carefully. Accordingly, all non-commercial mark-ups are reviewed by **Calder Stone Partners LLP** before being accepted or rejected by the desk.

Where Calder Stone confirms that a mark-up is purely clarificatory and does not alter commercial substance, the desk may accept the mark-up without escalation to the Credit Committee. Where Calder Stone identifies a mark-up that appears non-commercial but may have unintended commercial or legal consequences, the mark-up is treated as a substantive proposal and is addressed through the relevant section of this playbook.

In the Meridian negotiation, 16 of 23 total Turn 2 mark-ups were classified as non-commercial. Of the 14 marks addressed in the Fenn email of 4 April 2025, 7 were accepted (all of which were non-commercial). The remaining 9 unaddressed marks are pending Voss Bank Credit Committee review. Of these 9 unaddressed marks, the desk expects that a number will be reclassified as non-commercial upon further review, with the remainder being addressed as substantive issues in the Turn 3 redline.

**[Paragraph 4 --- Margin Maintenance]{.underline}**

**Paragraph 4(a) --- Margin Deficit / Margin Excess**

**4.1** The parties shall, on each Business Day (or at such other intervals as may be agreed), mark to market all outstanding Transactions by reference to the Market Value of the Purchased Securities and the Transaction Exposure in respect of each Transaction, each calculated in the Base Currency.

**4.2** If at any time the aggregate Cash Margin (if any) held by or on behalf of Buyer, together with the aggregate Market Value of all Purchased Securities held by Buyer (adjusted by the application of the relevant Haircut Percentage), is less than the aggregate Transaction Exposure of Buyer with respect to all Transactions then outstanding, a \"**Margin Deficit**\" shall be deemed to exist. The amount of such Margin Deficit shall be equal to the shortfall, calculated in the Base Currency.

**4.3** If at any time the aggregate Market Value of all Purchased Securities held by Buyer (adjusted by the application of the relevant Haircut Percentage), together with any Cash Margin held by or on behalf of Buyer, exceeds the aggregate Transaction Exposure of Buyer with respect to all Transactions then outstanding, a \"**Margin Excess**\" shall be deemed to exist. The amount of such Margin Excess shall be equal to the surplus, calculated in the Base Currency.

**Paragraph 4(b) --- Delivery Amount / Return Amount**

**4.4** Upon the existence of a Margin Deficit, Buyer may by notice to Seller (a \"**Margin Call**\") require Seller to transfer to Buyer Additional Purchased Securities or Cash Margin (or any combination thereof) in an amount sufficient to eliminate such Margin Deficit (the aggregate amount so required, the \"**Delivery Amount**\"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, no transfer shall be required if the Delivery Amount would be less than or equal to the applicable Margin Threshold specified in Annex II, Section 5(a) (being \$500,000 as of the date hereof).

**4.5** Upon the existence of a Margin Excess, Seller may by notice to Buyer (also a \"**Margin Call**\") require Buyer to transfer to Seller Equivalent Securities or Cash Margin (or any combination thereof) sufficient to eliminate such Margin Excess (the aggregate amount so required, the \"**Return Amount**\"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, no transfer shall be required if the Return Amount would be less than or equal to the applicable Margin Threshold specified in Annex II, Section 5(b) (being \$500,000 as of the date hereof).

**4.6** Any Additional Purchased Securities transferred by Seller to Buyer pursuant to a Margin Call must constitute Eligible Collateral, and the Market Value of such Additional Purchased Securities (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) shall be at least equal to the Delivery Amount.

**Paragraph 4(c) --- Margin Call Timing**

**4.7** A Margin Call must be received by the other party by the margin call cut-off time specified in Annex II, Section 7 (being 10:00 a.m. London time as of the date hereof) in order for the resulting transfer to be required on that same Business Day.

**4.8** If a Margin Call is received before the cut-off time on a Business Day, the party receiving the Margin Call shall make the required transfer on that same Business Day.

**4.9** If a Margin Call is received at or after the cut-off time on a Business Day, or on a day that is not a Business Day, the party receiving the Margin Call shall make the required transfer on the next following Business Day.

**4.10** For the purposes of this Paragraph 4(c), a Margin Call shall be deemed to have been \"received\" when it is actually received by the recipient at the address, facsimile number, or electronic mail address specified in Annex II, Section 14 for the giving of notices. Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to acknowledge receipt of a Margin Call promptly upon receipt.

**Paragraph 4(d) --- Haircuts**

**4.11** The applicable Haircut Percentage for each category of Eligible Collateral is as specified in Annex II, Section 4, and is summarised as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Category**                        **Haircut Percentage**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Eligible Sovereign Securities       1.5% (the \"Sovereign Haircut\")

  Eligible Corporate Securities       3.5% (the \"Corporate Haircut\")
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

**4.12** The Transaction Exposure in respect of any Transaction shall be calculated by applying the relevant Haircut Percentage to the Market Value of the Purchased Securities. The Haircut Percentage shall be applied in the manner set out in Annex II, Section 4, such that the Purchase Price for a Transaction shall be determined by dividing the Market Value of the Purchased Securities by one (1) plus the applicable Haircut Percentage (expressed as a decimal).

**4.13** Buyer reserves the right, upon not less than five (5) Business Days\' prior written notice to Seller, to revise the applicable Haircut Percentage for any category of Eligible Collateral in connection with future Transactions, provided that (a) any such revision shall apply only to Transactions entered into after the effective date of such revision and shall not affect the terms of any Transaction already outstanding, and (b) any such revision shall be made in good faith and on a commercially reasonable basis, having regard to prevailing market conditions, the credit quality of the relevant class of securities, and Buyer\'s internal risk management policies.

**[Paragraph 5 --- Income Payments]{.underline}**

**5.1** Where Purchased Securities are held by Buyer on a record date, ex-dividend date, or other relevant date for any distribution of Income (including, without limitation, any coupon, interest payment, dividend, principal repayment (other than at maturity), or other distribution payable in respect of such Purchased Securities), Buyer shall, on the next Business Day following the date on which Buyer receives or is credited with such Income, pay to Seller an amount equal to such Income (a \"**Manufactured Payment**\").

**[Paragraph 7 --- Netting of Obligations]{.underline}**

**Paragraph 7(a) --- Payment Netting**

**7.1** The standard payment netting provisions of the 2011 ICMA GMRA shall apply. Accordingly, where on any Business Day amounts would be payable by each party to the other in the same currency and on the same value date, the mutual obligations of each party to make any such payment shall be automatically satisfied and discharged and replaced by an obligation upon the party by whom the larger aggregate amount would have been payable to pay to the other party the excess of the larger aggregate amount over the smaller aggregate amount. Such single net payment shall be made by the party owing the net amount on the relevant value date in the manner specified in Paragraph 6(a).

**Paragraph 7(b) --- Close-out Netting / Settlement Netting**

**7.2** **Elected.** If on any day amounts would otherwise be payable in the same currency and in respect of the same settlement date by each party to the other (whether pursuant to Paragraph 4 (Margin Maintenance), Paragraph 5 (Income Payments), Paragraph 10 (Events of Default), or otherwise under this Agreement), the obligations of each party to make any such payment shall be automatically satisfied and discharged and, if the aggregate amount payable by one party exceeds the aggregate amount payable by the other party, replaced by an obligation upon the party by whom the larger aggregate amount would have been payable to pay to the other party the excess of the larger aggregate amount over the smaller aggregate amount.

**7.3** The single net amount determined in accordance with Paragraph 7.2 above shall be payable in the relevant currency on the relevant settlement date, and only the net amount shall be required to be paid by the party owing such amount. The other party shall have no obligation to make any payment in respect of the amounts so netted.

**7.4** Each party represents that the netting provisions of this Paragraph 7 are enforceable against it in all relevant jurisdictions, including the jurisdiction of its incorporation or organisation, the jurisdiction of its principal office, and any other jurisdiction in which it conducts business or holds assets. Each party agrees to take such steps and execute such documents as may reasonably be required to give effect to the netting provisions of this Paragraph 7.

Interest shall accrue on Cash Margin at the rate and on the basis specified in Annex II, or, if no such rate is specified, at the overnight interbank rate prevailing from time to time in the principal financial centre of the currency of the Cash Margin. The party holding Cash Margin shall pay interest thereon to the party that transferred such Cash Margin in accordance with the terms elected in Annex II.

**(f) Return of Excess Margin.** If at any time the Net Exposure of a party to whom a Margin Transfer has been made is reduced below the Threshold Amount (if any), or if the party that previously had the Net Exposure no longer has such exposure, the party holding the excess Margin Securities or Cash Margin shall, upon demand by the other party, transfer to the other party Equivalent Margin Securities and/or Cash Margin, as the case may be, in an amount sufficient to reduce the Net Value of Margin Provided to an amount not exceeding the current Net Exposure (after taking into account any Threshold Amount and Minimum Transfer Amount).

**(g) Timing of Margin Transfers.** Any Margin Transfer demanded in accordance with this Paragraph 4 shall be made by the close of business on the next Business Day following the date of the demand or such other time as the parties may agree. If the parties have agreed a different settlement cycle for Margin Transfers in Annex II, such agreed cycle shall apply.

**(h) Disputes Regarding Margin.** If the parties disagree as to the Market Value of any Securities, Cash Margin, or the amount of any Net Exposure, they shall use reasonable efforts to resolve such disagreement in good faith. Pending resolution of any such dispute:

> \(i\) the party upon whom a demand has been made shall transfer the undisputed amount of margin to the other party; and
>
> \(ii\) the parties shall seek to agree upon the Market Value of the relevant Securities by reference to independent pricing sources, and, failing such agreement, by reference to quotations obtained from not fewer than two independent market-makers or dealers in the relevant Securities. The average of such quotations shall be the Market Value for the purposes of this Paragraph 4.

**[Paragraph 5 --- Income Payments]{.underline}**

**(a) Buyer\'s Obligation.** Where Income is paid in respect of any Purchased Securities during the Term of a Transaction, Buyer shall, on the relevant Income Payment Date, or on such other date as the parties may agree, pay to Seller an amount equal to the amount of such Income as would have been received by Seller had the Purchased Securities not been the subject of such Transaction.

**(b) Timing of Income Payment.** Unless otherwise agreed between the parties, the amount referred to in sub-paragraph (a) above shall be paid on the date on which such Income is paid in respect of the relevant Securities by the issuer or the relevant paying agent. If Income is paid on a day that is not a Business Day, payment shall be made on the next following Business Day.

**(c) Manufactured Payments.** Where any payment under this Paragraph 5 constitutes a \"manufactured payment\" or \"manufactured dividend\" or similar payment for tax or regulatory purposes, the following provisions shall apply:

> \(i\) if Buyer is required by applicable law to withhold or deduct any amount from such payment on account of tax, Buyer shall make the relevant withholding or deduction and shall pay to Seller the net amount remaining after such withholding or deduction;
>
> \(ii\) unless otherwise agreed in Annex II, Buyer shall not be required to gross up or pay any additional amounts to compensate Seller for any such withholding or deduction; and
>
> \(iii\) the parties shall cooperate in good faith to minimise any such withholding or deduction and to provide such forms, certificates, or documentation as may be reasonably required by applicable law or regulation.

**(d) Set-off of Income.** Buyer may set off any amount due from Buyer to Seller under this Paragraph 5 against any amount due from Seller to Buyer under any Transaction, provided that both amounts are due and payable on the same date and are denominated in the same currency.

**(e) Buy/Sell Back Transactions.** In the case of Buy/Sell Back Transactions, the treatment of Income shall be as provided in Part 1 of Annex I. The Sell Back Price shall be adjusted to reflect any Income received or receivable during the Term, in accordance with the formula set out in Part 1 of Annex I, and the provisions of this Paragraph 5 shall apply only to the extent specified in Annex I and subject to any elections made in Annex II.

**[Paragraph 6 --- Payment and Transfer]{.underline}**

**(a) Payments.** All payments to be made under this Agreement shall be made in freely available, immediately available, same-day funds in the relevant Contractual Currency. Unless otherwise agreed between the parties, all payments shall be made not later than the time customary in the relevant market for payments in the Contractual Currency on the date on which such payment is due.

**(b) Deliveries of Securities.** All deliveries of Securities to be made under this Agreement shall be made through the clearing system or settlement system agreed between the parties in the relevant Confirmation or in Annex II, or, if no such system is specified, through such system as is customary for the settlement of transactions in such Securities. Deliveries may be made on a free of payment basis or on a delivery versus payment basis, as specified in the relevant Confirmation or as otherwise agreed.

**(c) Set-off and Payment Netting.** Where on any date amounts are due from each party to the other under two or more Transactions, and such amounts are denominated in the same currency, the parties may (and, if so elected in Annex II, shall) net such amounts so that only the net amount shall be payable by the party owing the larger aggregate amount. Each party\'s obligation to pay amounts under this Agreement on any date shall, to the extent of such netting, be discharged and replaced by the obligation of one party to pay the net amount to the other.

**(d) Default Interest.** If either party fails to pay any amount when due under this Agreement, interest shall accrue on such unpaid amount from (and including) the date on which such amount was due to (but excluding) the date of actual payment, at a rate per annum equal to the overnight cost of funding of the Non-Defaulting Party or the party to whom such amount is owed, as reasonably determined by such party, or at such other rate as may be agreed in Annex II. Such interest shall be payable on demand and shall be calculated on the basis of a year of 360 days (or 365 days, as applicable to the relevant currency) and the actual number of days elapsed.

**(e) Currency Conversion.** Where it is necessary for the purposes of this Agreement to convert any amount from one currency to another, such conversion shall be effected at the Spot Rate on the relevant date or, if no Spot Rate is available on such date, on the most recent date on which a Spot Rate is available, and any resulting amount shall be expressed in the Base Currency for the purpose of aggregation, comparison, or netting under this Agreement.

**[Paragraph 7 --- Contractual Currency]{.underline}**

**(a)** Each payment obligation arising under this Agreement shall be satisfied by payment in the Contractual Currency. If, for any reason, a party receives payment in a currency other than the Contractual Currency, and the amount received by such party, upon conversion to the Contractual Currency at the Spot Rate on the date of receipt, is less than the amount due in the Contractual Currency, the paying party shall remain liable for the shortfall. If the amount received upon such conversion exceeds the amount due, the receiving party shall not be obliged to refund the excess, but may, at its discretion, credit such excess against future payment obligations of the paying party.

**(b)** The obligation to pay any shortfall arising under sub-paragraph (a) above shall constitute a separate and independent obligation of the paying party, enforceable irrespective of any judgment or order obtained or made in respect of the original payment obligation or any other obligation under this Agreement. This obligation shall not be affected by any judgment or order that may be expressed or converted into a currency other than the Contractual Currency.

**(c)** For the purposes of this Paragraph 7, the conversion rate to be applied shall be the Spot Rate on the date on which conversion is made. Where multiple conversions are required, each such conversion shall be effected at the Spot Rate prevailing on the date of the relevant conversion.

**[Paragraph 8 --- Substitution]{.underline}**

**(a) Right to Request Substitution.** Subject to the terms of this Paragraph 8, Seller may at any time during the Term of a Transaction request Buyer to accept substitute securities (\"**New Purchased Securities**\") in place of all or any part of the existing Purchased Securities, and Buyer shall not unreasonably withhold or delay its consent to such substitution. Buyer shall be entitled to refuse consent to a substitution if the proposed New Purchased Securities are not reasonably acceptable to Buyer having regard to the creditworthiness of the issuer, the liquidity of the market for such securities, the type or category of securities, or any other commercially reasonable ground.

**(b) Mechanics of Substitution.** If Buyer consents to a substitution, the substitution shall be effected by the simultaneous transfer by Seller to Buyer of the New Purchased Securities and the transfer by Buyer to Seller of the existing Purchased Securities (or such portion thereof as is being substituted), or by such other arrangement as the parties may agree. Upon such substitution, all references in this Agreement and in the relevant Confirmation to \"Purchased Securities\" shall, in respect of the relevant Transaction, be deemed to refer to the New Purchased Securities, and the terms of the Transaction shall be adjusted accordingly.

**(c) Equivalent Value.** The New Purchased Securities shall have a Market Value as at the date of substitution that is substantially the same as (or, if so agreed between the parties, not less than) the Market Value of the Purchased Securities they replace, determined as at the same date. If the Market Value of the New Purchased Securities is less than the Market Value of the Purchased Securities being replaced, Seller shall transfer additional Securities or Cash Margin in an amount sufficient to eliminate the shortfall, or the parties shall agree such other adjustments to the Transaction as are appropriate.

**(d) Effect on Margin.** Following any substitution, the margin obligations of the parties under Paragraph 4 shall be recalculated by reference to the Market Value of the New Purchased Securities. Any Margin Transfer demand outstanding prior to such substitution shall be adjusted accordingly, and any Margin Transfer already made shall be taken into account in the recalculated margin position.

**(a) Power and Authority.** Each party represents and warrants to the other party (on the date of this Agreement and as at each date specified in sub-paragraph (f) below) that it has the power, authority, and legal right to enter into this Agreement and each Transaction under this Agreement, and to perform its obligations hereunder and thereunder.

**(e) Title.** Seller represents and warrants to Buyer, in respect of each Transaction, that at the time of transfer of Purchased Securities to Buyer on the Purchase Date, Seller has the full and unqualified right to sell and transfer such Securities free and clear of any lien, charge, claim, security interest, encumbrance, right of set-off, or any other adverse interest or claim of any third party.

**(f) Repetition.** The representations and warranties made by each party under this Paragraph 9 shall be deemed to be repeated by such party on each Purchase Date, on each date on which a Transaction is outstanding, and on each date on which a Margin Transfer is made or received.

**[Paragraph 10 --- Events of Default; Remedies]{.underline}**

**(a) Events of Default.** Each of the following events shall constitute an \"**Event of Default**\" with respect to a party (the \"**Defaulting Party**\"):

> \(i\) **Failure to Pay Purchase Price or Repurchase Price.** Buyer fails to pay the Purchase Price on the Purchase Date or Seller fails to pay the Repurchase Price on the Repurchase Date, and such failure is not remedied within the number of Business Days specified as the cure period in Annex II (or, if no such period is specified, on or before the next Business Day following notice from the Non-Defaulting Party);

> \(ii\) **Failure to Deliver Securities.** Seller fails to deliver the Purchased Securities on the Purchase Date or Buyer fails to deliver Equivalent Securities on the Repurchase Date, and such failure is not remedied within the number of Business Days specified as the cure period in Annex II (or, if no such period is specified, on or before the next Business Day following notice from the Non-Defaulting Party);
>
> \(iii\) **Failure to Pay Income.** Buyer fails to pay any amount due under Paragraph 5 (Income Payments) when due, and such failure is not remedied within the number of Business Days specified as the cure period in Annex II (or, if no such period is specified, on or before the next Business Day following notice from the Non-Defaulting Party);

> \(iv\) **Failure to Make Margin Transfer.** A party fails to make a Margin Transfer as required under Paragraph 4 when due, and such failure is not remedied within the number of Business Days specified as the cure period in Annex II (or, if no such period is specified, on or before the next Business Day following notice from the Non-Defaulting Party);
>
> \(v\) **Act of Insolvency.** An Act of Insolvency occurs in respect of either party;
>
> \(vi\s Agreement in favour of a central bank or monetary authority, subject to applicable law.

**(b) Termination of Agreement.** Either party may terminate this Agreement by giving not fewer than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other party, provided that:

> \(ii\) all obligations of each party to the other under this Agreement (including, without limitation, payment and delivery obligations, margin obligations, and obligations in respect of Transaction Costs and interest) have been fully discharged; and

> \(iii\) no Event of Default has occurred and is continuing in respect of either party.

**[Supplemental Terms and Conditions]{.underline}**

**Part 1 --- Buy/Sell Back Transactions**

**1.1 Definition and Characteristics.** A \"Buy/Sell Back Transaction\" is a Transaction in which one party (the Seller) agrees to sell Securities to the other party (the Buyer) on the Purchase Date, and the Buyer agrees to sell Equivalent Securities to the Seller on the Repurchase Date, where:

> \(a\) the economic effect of the transaction is equivalent to that of a repurchase transaction, but the transaction is documented and settled as a pair of outright sale and purchase transactions;
>
> \(b\) title to the Purchased Securities passes absolutely from Seller to Buyer on the Purchase Date, and title to the Equivalent Securities passes absolutely from Buyer to Seller on the Repurchase Date;
>
> \(c\) the price payable by Seller for the Equivalent Securities on the Repurchase Date (the Sell Back Price) is determined in accordance with the formula set out in this Part 1 of Annex I and reflects the economic terms of the financing effected by the Transaction; and
>
> \(d\) the Transaction is identified as a Buy/Sell Back Transaction in the relevant Confirmation or is otherwise agreed by the parties to be a Buy/Sell Back Transaction.

A Buy/Sell Back Transaction is distinguished from a standard repurchase transaction principally by the manner in which the Repurchase Price is calculated (i.e., as a Sell Back Price determined by a pricing formula) and by the treatment of Income arising during the Term.

**1.2 Pricing Mechanics: Calculation of the Sell Back Price.** The Sell Back Price for a Buy/Sell Back Transaction shall be calculated in accordance with the following formula:

> **Sell Back Price = Purchase Price × (1 + (Pricing Rate × n / D)) -- IC**

Where:

> • **Purchase Price** is the price paid by the Buyer to the Seller on the Purchase Date;
>
> • **Pricing Rate** is the per annum percentage rate agreed between the parties for the Transaction;
>
> • **n** is the actual number of days from (and including) the Purchase Date to (but excluding) the Repurchase Date;
>
> • **D** is 360 or 365, as applicable to the day count convention for the relevant currency (or as otherwise agreed between the parties); and
>
> • **IC** is the aggregate amount of Income (if any) paid or received during the Term in respect of the Purchased Securities, together with any reinvestment return on such Income calculated in accordance with sub-paragraph 1.3 below.

The parties may agree to use an alternative pricing formula, provided that such alternative is specified in the relevant Confirmation.

**1.3 Income Treatment.** Where any Income is paid or received in respect of the Purchased Securities during the Term of a Buy/Sell Back Transaction:

> \(a\) the Sell Back Price shall be adjusted to reflect such Income, in accordance with the formula set out in sub-paragraph 1.2 above;
>
> \(b\) the adjustment shall take into account any reinvestment return on such Income, calculated by reference to the Pricing Rate (or such other rate as may be agreed) from the date on which such Income is paid to (but excluding) the Repurchase Date;
>
> \(c\) the obligation of the Buyer to make a manufactured payment under Paragraph 5 shall not apply to a Buy/Sell Back Transaction (unless otherwise agreed in Annex II), as the Income treatment is reflected in the calculation of the Sell Back Price; and
>
> \(d\) if Income is paid in a currency other than the currency of the Purchase Price, the parties shall agree the applicable exchange rate for the purposes of the adjustment, or, in the absence of agreement, the Spot Rate on the date on which such Income is paid shall apply.

**1.4 Title Transfer.** Title to the Purchased Securities shall pass absolutely from Seller to Buyer on the Purchase Date, and the Buyer shall have the unrestricted right to deal with and dispose of the Purchased Securities during the Term. Title to the Equivalent Securities shall pass absolutely from Buyer to Seller on the Repurchase Date upon payment of the Sell Back Price by Seller.

**1.5 Confirmation Requirements.** In addition to the terms specified in Paragraph 3(a), the Confirmation for a Buy/Sell Back Transaction shall set out:

> \(a\) a statement that the Transaction is a Buy/Sell Back Transaction;
>
> \(b\) the Sell Back Price (or the method by which the Sell Back Price is to be calculated);
>
> \(c\) the Pricing Rate;
>
> \(d\) the applicable day count convention;
>
> \(e\) any specific provisions for the treatment of Income; and
>
> \(f\) such other terms as the parties may agree.

**1.6 Application of Margin Maintenance.** The provisions of Paragraph 4 (Margin Maintenance) shall apply to Buy/Sell Back Transactions only if the parties have elected in Part 2 of Annex II that margin maintenance shall apply to Buy/Sell Back Transactions. If such election has been made, references in Paragraph 4 to \"Repurchase Price\" shall, in relation to a Buy/Sell Back Transaction, be construed as references to the Sell Back Price as at the relevant date.

**1.7 Events of Default.** The provisions of Paragraph 10 (Events of Default; Remedies) shall apply to Buy/Sell Back Transactions. In applying such provisions, references to the \"Repurchase Price\" shall be construed as references to the \"Sell Back Price,\" and references to \"Equivalent Securities\" shall have the corresponding meaning applicable to Buy/Sell Back Transactions.

**1.8 Modifications.** To the extent that any of the provisions of Paragraphs 3 through 10 are inconsistent with the characteristics of a Buy/Sell Back Transaction as described in this Part 1 of Annex I, the provisions of this Part 1 shall prevail in relation to such Transaction.

**Part 2 --- Agency Transactions**

**2.1 General.** This Part 2 applies to Transactions entered into by a party (the \"**Agent**\") acting as agent on behalf of one or more principals (each a \"**Principal**\"). An Agency Transaction is a Transaction identified as such in the relevant Confirmation or otherwise agreed by the parties to be an Agency Transaction.

**2.2 Disclosure Requirements.** The Agent shall, at or before the time of entering into an Agency Transaction, disclose to the other party (the \"**Counterparty**\"):

> \(a\) that it is acting in the capacity of agent on behalf of a Principal; and
>
> \(b\) the identity of the Principal on whose behalf it is acting, unless the parties have agreed in Annex II that the Agent need not disclose the identity of the Principal.

If the Agent fails to disclose its agency capacity to the Counterparty at or before the time of entering into the Transaction, the Agent shall be treated as having entered into such Transaction as principal and shall be liable to the Counterparty as principal thereunder.

**2.3 Liability of Agent.** Where the Agent has disclosed its agency capacity and the identity of the Principal:

> \(a\) the Agent shall incur no personal liability to the Counterparty in respect of the Agency Transaction, provided that the Agent has acted within the scope of its authority as agent for the Principal;
>
> \(b\) the Counterparty\'s credit risk in respect of the Agency Transaction shall be to the Principal and not to the Agent;
>
> \(c\) the Agent represents that it has the authority of the Principal to enter into the Agency Transaction on the terms set out in the relevant Confirmation and this Agreement; and
>
> \(d\) the Agent shall be liable to the Counterparty for any loss or damage suffered by the Counterparty as a result of the Agent having acted in excess of its authority, unless the Principal has ratified the Agent\'s actions.

**2.4 Application of Netting and Set-off.** In respect of Agency Transactions:

> \(a\) the close-out netting provisions of Paragraph 10 shall apply between the Principal and the Counterparty (and not between the Agent and the Counterparty, except where the Agent is also acting as principal in respect of other Transactions);
>
> \(b\) the Counterparty may not net or set off amounts due from or to one Principal against amounts due from or to any other Principal, even if the same Agent is acting on behalf of more than one Principal; and
>
> \(c\) the margin maintenance provisions of Paragraph 4 shall apply separately in respect of each Principal.

**2.5 Events of Default.** In relation to Agency Transactions:

> \(a\) an Event of Default shall be determined by reference to the Principal (not the Agent), except to the extent that the Event of Default arises from the Agent\'s failure to perform obligations within the scope of its own duties (such as failure to deliver confirmations or to transmit payments);
>
> \(b\) an Act of Insolvency in respect of the Agent shall not of itself constitute an Event of Default in respect of any Principal, unless the Agent is also a party to Transactions in its own capacity; and
>
> \(c\) the parties may agree in Annex II to additional provisions governing Events of Default in respect of Agency Transactions.

**2.6 Representations by Agent.** The Agent represents and warrants to the Counterparty that:

> \(a\) it has the authority of each relevant Principal to enter into each Agency Transaction on behalf of such Principal;
>
> \(b\) each Agency Transaction constitutes a valid and binding obligation of the relevant Principal enforceable in accordance with its terms;
>
> \(c\) the Agent\'s authority has not been revoked, limited, or qualified in any manner that would affect its ability to enter into the Agency Transaction; and
>
> \(d\) the Agent has disclosed all material information regarding its agency capacity and the identity of the Principal (to the extent required).

**Part 3 --- Additional Supplemental Terms**

**3.1 Provisions for Specific Securities Types.** The parties may, in a Confirmation or by agreement in Annex II, modify or supplement the terms of this Agreement in relation to Transactions involving specific types of Securities, including, without limitation:

> \(a\) equities and equity-linked securities (including provisions relating to corporate actions, voting rights, and the treatment of dividends);
>
> \(b\) gilts and other government bonds (including provisions relating to the specific settlement conventions and Income Payment Dates applicable to such securities);
>
> \(c\) asset-backed securities, mortgage-backed securities, and similar instruments (including provisions relating to prepayment risk and the treatment of principal repayments); and
>
> \(d\) any other category of Securities that may require specific or modified provisions.

**3.2 Additional Transaction Types.** The parties may agree to apply this Agreement to additional categories of transactions not otherwise described in this Agreement or in Part 1 or Part 2 of this Annex I, by specifying the additional terms and conditions applicable to such transactions in a Confirmation or by agreement in Annex II.

**3.3 Modifications to Definitions.** Where the parties enter into Transactions involving Securities or in markets for which the definitions in Paragraph 2 require modification or supplementation, such modifications or supplementations shall be set out in the relevant Confirmation or in Annex II and shall be deemed to form part of the definitions in Paragraph 2 for the purposes of such Transactions.

**3.4 Other Supplemental Terms.** Any other supplemental terms and conditions modifying or adding to the printed paragraphs of this Agreement may be agreed by the parties and set out in Annex II, in a side letter, or in the relevant Confirmation, and shall be incorporated into and form part of this Agreement.

109: eridian's ability to comply with those regulatory obligations. Importantly, M=
110: eridian's proposed mechanics would still require that any substituted collate=
111: ral fall within the same or better Eligible Collateral category and that no M=

117: ay of any Transaction. Meridian's Turn 2 counter deletes the in-term repricin=
118: g right, such that repricing would be available only at maturity roll. In-ter=

Alistair,
I hope this finds you well. As you know, Pryor, Ashworth & Gelb LLP acts on b=
ehalf of Meridian Capital Securities LLC (the "Seller") in connection with th=
e negotiation of a 2011 ICMA Global Master Repurchase Agreement (with 2011 An=
nex I) between Meridian and Voss Bank AG, acting through its London Branch (t=
he "Buyer"). We refer to the Turn 1 draft circulated by Calder Stone on behal=
f of Voss Bank on 14 March 2025.
Please find attached our Turn 2 redline (filename: turn-2-redline-meridian.do=
cx), marked against the Turn 1 draft. The redline contains 23 mark-ups in tot=
al. Of these, 16 are non-commercial or drafting in nature =E2=80=94 correctio=
ns to defined terms, cross-references, clarifications, and the like =E2=80=94=
while 7 raise substantive commercial points. I have set out a summary of eac=
h of the commercial issues below, together with Meridian's rationale, in the =
hope that this is helpful in framing a productive discussion.
**Party Identifiers and Annex I Elections**
Before turning to the commercial issues, I can confirm that the following ele=
ctions and identifiers are reflected in Turn 2:
- **Buyer:** Voss Bank AG, London Branch; FCA FRN 487203; CHE-314.827.059; LE=
I 2138004WJZ83NHQKF744
- **Seller:** Meridian Capital Securities LLC; CRD# 298417; EIN 83-2947561; L=
EI 5493007XKBT49LP2QR12
- **Base Currency:** USD
- **Buy/Sell Back Transactions:** Not Applicable
- **Agency Transactions:** Not Applicable
- **Netting:** Paragraph 7(b) elected =E2=80=94 same-currency, same-settlemen=
t-date
- **Tax Gross-Up:** Paragraph 11(b) elected; 5 business day cure period (per =
Annex II election); failure to cure constitutes an Event of Default
- **Income Payment:** Manufactured Payments due next business day following t=
he record date
- **Settlement:** Clearstream Banking S.A. for EUR-denominated Eligible Colla=
teral; The Depository Trust Company (DTC) for USD-denominated Eligible Collat=
eral. Settlement is bilateral; no tri-party custodian is elected at this time=
, though we note that BNY Meliora Trust Company, N.A. remains available shoul=
d the parties later elect to adopt the tri-party annexe
- **Net Exposure Cap:** $1,500,000,000 (unchanged from Turn 1)
- **Margin Call Cut-Off:** 10:00 a.m. London time; calls received before cut-=
off settle same day; calls received at or after cut-off settle on the next bu=
siness day
The Eligible Collateral criteria are carried forward from Turn 1 without chan=
ge: (i) sovereign obligations of G7 nations (United States, United Kingdom, G=
ermany, France, Japan, Canada, Italy), rated A=E2=80=93 (S&P) / A3 (Moody's) =
or above; and (ii) corporate obligations rated BBB+ (S&P) / Baa1 (Moody's) or=
above, with residual maturity of 10 years or less.
**Summary of Key Commercial Issues**
**1. Haircuts =E2=80=94 Sovereign Collateral**
The Turn 1 draft provides for a 2.0% haircut on sovereign collateral. Meridia=
n's Turn 2 counter is 1.5%. In Meridian's view, a 2.0% haircut for G7 soverei=
gn collateral rated A=E2=80=93 or above sits above current market convention =
for investment-grade sovereign repo on a dealer-to-dealer basis, and 1.5% bet=
ter reflects prevailing pricing. To illustrate the practical impact: at a Mar=
ket Value of $100,000,000, a 1.5% haircut yields a Purchase Price of approxim=
ately $98,522,167.49, whereas a 2.0% haircut yields approximately $98,039,215=
.69 =E2=80=94 a difference of roughly $483,000 per $100 million. That said, M=
eridian is open to discussing a midpoint if that would be helpful.
**2. Haircuts =E2=80=94 Corporate Collateral**
The Turn 1 draft provides for a 5.0% haircut on corporate collateral. Meridia=
n's Turn 2 counter is 3.5%. The eligible corporate universe is already limite=
d to BBB+/Baa1 and above with a residual maturity of 10 years or less, which =
significantly mitigates both credit and duration risk. Against those constrai=
nts, a 5.0% haircut provides excessive over-collateralisation. By way of illu=
stration: at a Market Value of $50,000,000, a 3.5% haircut yields a Purchase =
Price of approximately $48,309,178.74, versus approximately $47,619,047.62 at=
**3. Margin Threshold**
The Turn 1 draft sets a symmetric margin threshold of $250,000 (applicable to=
both Buyer and Seller deliveries). Meridian's Turn 2 counter is $500,000, al=
so symmetric. A $250,000 threshold is operationally burdensome for a portfoli=
o that could reach the $1.5 billion Net Exposure Cap, and would likely genera=
te frequent small margin calls with limited credit benefit. A $500,000 thresh=
old reduces operational friction without materially increasing credit exposur=
e for either party. We would note that Meridian is also willing to discuss an=
asymmetric structure if that better addresses Voss Bank's particular concern=
s.
**4. Substitution of Collateral**
The Turn 1 draft requires the prior written consent of the Buyer for any subs=
titution of collateral. Meridian's Turn 2 counter provides the Seller with a =
unilateral right to substitute on one business day's notice. The Buyer's cons=
ent requirement is, with respect, inconsistent with industry-standard substit=
ution mechanics for broker-dealer counterparties. As a registered broker-deal=
er (CRD# 298417), Meridian is subject to SEC net capital requirements and mus=
t retain the ability to manage its inventory and collateral pool actively. Re=
quiring prior written consent for each substitution could materially impair M=
eridian's ability to comply with those regulatory obligations. Importantly, M=
eridian's proposed mechanics would still require that any substituted collate=
ral fall within the same or better Eligible Collateral category and that no M=
argin Deficit exists at the time of substitution.
**5. Repricing**
The Turn 1 draft grants the Buyer an option to reprice on the 90th calendar d=
ay of any Transaction. Meridian's Turn 2 counter deletes the in-term repricin=
g right, such that repricing would be available only at maturity roll. In-ter=
m repricing introduces uncertainty around carry economics and complicates Mer=
idian's hedging and funding cost calculations; Meridian's strong preference i=
s accordingly to limit repricing to the point of roll. That said, Meridian ac=
knowledges that Voss Bank may have legitimate concerns regarding term trades =
with extended tenors, and we would be willing to discuss a compromise that ba=
lances certainty of pricing against market-movement risk =E2=80=94 for exampl=
e, a longer minimum period before repricing is triggered, with adequate prior=
notice to the Seller.
**6. Cross-Default Threshold**
The Turn 1 draft sets a cross-default threshold of $10,000,000. Meridian's Tu=
rn 2 counter is $50,000,000. A $10,000,000 threshold represents only approxim=
ately 2.43% of Meridian's audited net capital of $412,000,000 (as of 31 Decem=
ber 2024), which is disproportionately low and could trigger an Event of Defa=
ult on the basis of routine commercial disputes or contested obligations that=
are immaterial to Meridian's creditworthiness. The Seller's counter of $50,0=
00,000 =E2=80=94 approximately 12.14% of net capital =E2=80=94 is more propor=
tionate to Meridian's balance sheet. Meridian would be willing to explore a f=
igure in the range of $25 million to $50 million.
**7. Act of Insolvency Grace Period**
The Turn 1 draft provides for zero days' grace =E2=80=94 i.e., an immediate E=
vent of Default upon an Act of Insolvency. Meridian's Turn 2 counter is a 30-=
calendar-day grace period. A zero-day grace period creates a real risk of pre=
mature termination based on erroneous filings or contested proceedings that m=
ay ultimately be dismissed. This concern is particularly acute for a US-domic=
iled counterparty, where involuntary bankruptcy petitions may be filed by cre=
ditors and subsequently vacated. A 30-calendar-day cure period allows suffici=
ent time to address frivolous or erroneous filings while still affording Voss=
Bank meaningful protection. We acknowledge that 30 days is toward the longer=
end of market practice and are open to discussing a shorter period =E2=80=94=
for example, 10 to 15 business days =E2=80=94 if that would be more acceptab=
le.
**Dispute Resolution and Governing Law**
Although not among the seven principal commercial issues above, I should also=
flag that while Meridian accepts English law as the governing law (no object=
ion), our Turn 2 redline proposes English High Court non-exclusive jurisdicti=
on in place of the LCIA arbitration clause in the Turn 1 draft. Meridian's co=
ncern is a practical one: as a US broker-dealer, enforcement of an LCIA award=
in US courts under the New York Convention, while generally reliable, introd=
uces additional procedural steps and potential litigation risk compared to di=
rect enforcement of an English court judgment. Non-exclusive jurisdiction pre=
serves optionality for both parties. We recognise, however, that Voss Bank ma=
y have reasons =E2=80=94 including confidentiality =E2=80=94 for preferring a=
rbitration, and Meridian would be prepared to discuss a compromise: for examp=
le, retaining LCIA arbitration as the general dispute resolution mechanism wi=
th an expedited procedure for lower-value claims.
**Non-Commercial and Drafting Mark-ups**
The remaining 16 mark-ups are non-commercial in nature. They include correcti=
ons to defined terms, cross-references, paragraph numbering, representation l=
anguage, and notice provisions =E2=80=94 including updated addresses for Meri=
dian's principal office at 200 Vesey Street, 38th Floor, New York, NY 10281 a=
nd its registered agent at Corporation Service Company, 251 Little Falls Driv=
e, Wilmington, DE 19808 =E2=80=94 as well as other conforming changes. We exp=
ect these should be largely non-controversial and would suggest that Miguel a=
nd Sana coordinate on these in parallel so that we can keep the focus of any =
principal-level discussion on the commercial points.
**Next Steps**
We would welcome a call in the week of 31 March or 7 April to discuss the sev=
en commercial issues summarised above. It would be helpful to have Dana Caste=
llano on our side, and I understand you may wish to include Lindqvist from Vo=
ss Bank's side. We are flexible on timing and happy to accommodate the London=
/New York time difference =E2=80=94 please let us know what works for your te=
am. Meridian's objective is to agree the remaining commercial terms and move =
to a Turn 3 redline as promptly as possible thereafter.
Thank you, Alistair. We look forward to hearing from you.
With best regards,
Rachel S. Okonkwo

I’ll write a Python script to list the zip files and target the word/document.xml. It might be better to extract text to a scratch file, count paragraphs, and include the inserted and deleted text. Bash commands could be useful for copying and unzipping too!
