84: P83: 5.3 All Manufactured Payments shall be made net of any applicable withholding tax, deduction, or other amount required to be withheld or deducted by Buyer under applicable law. If Buyer is required by applicable law to make any such withholding or deduction, the provisions of Paragraph 11 (Tax) shall apply with respect to any obligation of Buyer to gross up such payment.
85: P84: 5.4 For the avoidance of doubt, the obligation to make a Manufactured Payment arises regardless of whether Buyer has actually received the relevant Income payment from the issuer of the Purchased Securities. Buyer's obligation to make the Manufactured Payment is an independent obligation under this Agreement and shall not be conditional upon Buyer's receipt of the underlying Income.
86: P85: 5.5 In respect of any partial coupon period, the Manufactured Payment shall be calculated on an actual/actual (ICMA) day-count basis for Eligible Sovereign Securities and a 30/360 basis for Eligible Corporate Securities, unless otherwise specified in the relevant Confirmation.
87: P86: Paragraph 6 — Payment and Transfer
88: P87: Paragraph 6(a) — Method
89: P88: 6.1 All payments of cash required to be made under this Agreement shall be made in immediately available, freely transferable, same-day funds in the relevant currency to the account specified by the receiving party in the relevant Confirmation, in Annex II, Section 14, or as otherwise notified by the receiving party to the paying party in writing from time to time.
90: P89: 6.2 All transfers of Securities required to be made under this Agreement (including the initial transfer of Purchased Securities, the transfer of Additional Purchased Securities, the return of Equivalent Securities, and the transfer of Alternative Securities upon substitution) shall be made through the applicable settlement system, as follows:
91: P90: (a) For Euro-denominated Eligible Collateral: Clearstream Banking S.A., in accordance with the rules and procedures of Clearstream Banking S.A. as in effect from time to time.
92: P91: (b) For USD-denominated Eligible Collateral: The Depository Trust Company (DTC), in accordance with the rules and procedures of DTC as in effect from time to time.
93: P92: 6.3 Each party shall bear its own costs and expenses in connection with the settlement of Securities through the applicable settlement system, including any fees or charges imposed by the settlement system operator, the relevant custodian, or any intermediary in the settlement chain, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the parties.
94: P93: 6.4 Unless otherwise agreed between the parties for a specific Transaction, all deliveries of Securities shall be made on a delivery-versus-payment (DvP) basis. If DvP settlement is not available or practicable for a particular Transaction, the parties shall agree in advance on an alternative delivery mechanism and shall cooperate in good faith to minimise settlement risk.
95: P94: Paragraph 6(b) — Netting
96: P95: 6.5 As elected in Annex II, Section 8, Paragraph 7(b) of this Agreement (settlement netting for obligations in the same currency falling due on the same settlement date) shall apply. The parties agree that, where on any Business Day amounts would otherwise be payable in the same currency and on the same settlement date by each party to the other (whether under Paragraph 4, Paragraph 5, or otherwise under this Agreement), such obligations shall be subject to the netting provisions set out in Paragraph 7 below.
97: P96: Paragraph 7 — Netting of Obligations
98: P97: Paragraph 7(a) — Payment Netting
99: P98: 7.1 The standard payment netting provisions of the 2011 ICMA GMRA shall apply. Accordingly, where on any Business Day amounts would be payable by each party to the other in the same currency and on the same value date, the mutual obligations of each party to make any such payment shall be automatically satisfied and discharged and replaced by an obligation upon the party by whom the larger aggregate amount would have been payable to pay to the other party the excess of the larger aggregate amount over the smaller aggregate amount. Such single net payment shall be made by the party owing the net amount on the relevant value date in the manner specified in Paragraph 6(a).
100: P99: Paragraph 7(b) — Close-out Netting / Settlement Netting
101: P100: 7.2 Elected. If on any day amounts would otherwise be payable in the same currency and in respect of the same settlement date by each party to the other (whether pursuant to Paragraph 4 (Margin Maintenance), Paragraph 5 (Income Payments), Paragraph 10 (Events of Default), or otherwise under this Agreement), the obligations of each party to make any such payment shall be automatically satisfied and discharged and, if the aggregate amount payable by one party exceeds the aggregate amount payable by the other party, replaced by an obligation upon the party by whom the larger aggregate amount would have been payable to pay to the other party the excess of the larger aggregate amount over the smaller aggregate amount.
102: P101: 7.3 The single net amount determined in accordance with Paragraph 7.2 above shall be payable in the relevant currency on the relevant settlement date, and only the net amount shall be required to be paid by the party owing such amount. The other party shall have no obligation to make any payment in respect of the amounts so netted.
103: P102: 7.4 Each party represents that the netting provisions of this Paragraph 7 are enforceable against it in all relevant jurisdictions, including the jurisdiction of its incorporation or organisation, the jurisdiction of its principal office, and any other jurisdiction in which it conducts business or holds assets. Each party agrees to take such steps and execute such documents as may reasonably be required to give effect to the netting provisions of this Paragraph 7.
104: P103: Paragraph 8 — Substitution
105: P104: 8.1 Subject to the provisions of Annex II, Section 9, Seller may from time to time during the term of any Transaction request the substitution effect a substitution of Alternative Securities for all or any part of the Purchased Securities in that Transaction.
106: P105: 8.2 Any request for substitution notice of substitution shall be made by Seller to Buyer in writing (including by electronic mail) and shall specify the Purchased Securities to be replaced, the proposed Alternative Securities, and the proposed date on which the substitution is to take effect. The request notice shall include sufficient detail regarding the proposed Alternative Securities (including ISIN, nominal amount, issuer, coupon, maturity, and credit rating) to enable Buyer to evaluate the request proposed substitution.
107: P106: 8.3 Buyer's prior written consent is required for any substitution. Buyer may grant, withhold, condition, or delay such consent in its sole and absolute discretion. Buyer shall not be required to provide any reason for any refusal of a request for substitution. Buyer shall use reasonable efforts to respond to any request for substitution within two (2) Business Days of receipt, but any failure to respond within such period shall not constitute consent.
108: P107: 8.3 Seller shall give Buyer not less than one (1) Business Day's prior notice of any proposed substitution. No consent of Buyer shall be required.
109: P108: 8.4 Where Buyer has given its consent, the The substitution shall be effected on the Business Day agreed by the parties (or, failing agreement, on the second Business Day following the date of Buyer's consent) specified in Seller's notice by the simultaneous transfer of the Alternative Securities by Seller to Buyer (or to Buyer's account at the relevant settlement system) and the transfer of the relevant Purchased Securities by Buyer to Seller (or to Seller's account at the relevant settlement system), in each case in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 6.
110: P109: 8.5 Any Alternative Securities transferred by Seller must qualify as Eligible Collateral and must satisfy all of the eligibility criteria set out in Annex II, Section 3. The Market Value of the Alternative Securities (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) must be at least equal to the Market Value of the Purchased Securities being replaced (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) as of the close of business on the Business Day immediately preceding the substitution date.
111: P110: 8.6 Upon completion of a substitution, the Alternative Securities shall become the Purchased Securities for all purposes of the relevant Transaction, and the Confirmation for such Transaction shall be deemed to have been amended accordingly.
112: P111: Paragraph 9 — Representations
113: P112: 9.1 Each party represents and warrants to the other, as of the date of this Agreement and as of each Purchase Date on which it enters into a Transaction, that:
114: P113: (a) Due Organisation and Authority. It is duly organised, validly existing, and in good standing (or the equivalent) under the laws of its jurisdiction of incorporation or organisation. It has the full power and authority to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under this Agreement and each Transaction, and has taken all necessary corporate, regulatory, or other action to authorise such execution, delivery, and performance.
115: P114: (b) No Violation. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and each Transaction do not and will not (i) violate or conflict with any provision of its constitutional or organisational documents (including, without limitation, its memorandum and articles of association, certificate of formation, limited liability company agreement, partnership agreement, or equivalent documents), (ii) violate or conflict with any applicable law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree of any governmental authority or regulatory body having jurisdiction over it, or (iii) result in a breach of, or constitute a default under, any agreement, instrument, or obligation to which it is a party or by which it or any of its assets may be bound.
116: P115: (c) Governmental and Regulatory Approvals. All governmental and regulatory consents, approvals, authorisations, registrations, filings, and notices that are necessary for the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and each Transaction have been obtained or made and are in full force and effect.
117: P116: (d) Binding Obligations. This Agreement and each Transaction constitute legal, valid, and binding obligations of such party, enforceable against it in accordance with their respective terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganisation, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors' rights generally and to equitable principles of general applicability.
118: P117: (e) No Litigation. There is no pending or, to the best of its knowledge, threatened action, suit, proceeding, inquiry, or investigation before or by any court, tribunal, governmental authority, or regulatory body which would materially affect its ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement or any Transaction, or which questions the validity or enforceability of this Agreement or any Transaction.
119: P118: (f) Accuracy of Information. All information furnished by it to the other party in connection with this Agreement and each Transaction is true, accurate, and complete in all material respects as of the date on which such information is furnished, and it is not aware of any fact or circumstance that has not been disclosed to the other party and that might reasonably be expected to materially affect its ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement or any Transaction.
120: P119: (g) Internal Approvals. It has obtained all internal credit committee and risk committee approvals necessary for the execution of this Agreement and for entry into Transactions hereunder.
121: P120: 9.2 Additional Seller Representation. Meridian Capital Securities LLC represents and warrants, as of the date of this Agreement and as of each Purchase Date, that it is duly registered as a broker-dealer with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under Section 15 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and is a member in good standing of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), CRD# 298417. Seller further represents that its registration and membership are in full force and effect, that it is not subject to any suspension, revocation, or restriction on its registration or membership that would materially affect its ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement, and that it is in compliance in all material respects with all applicable requirements of the SEC and FINRA. Seller further represents that it is in compliance in all material respects with the net capital requirements of Rule 15c3-1 under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and covenants that it shall promptly notify Buyer in writing if its net capital falls below 120% of the minimum amount required under Rule 15c3-1.
122: P121: 9.3 Additional Buyer Representation. Voss Bank AG represents and warrants, as of the date of this Agreement and as of each Purchase Date, that it is duly authorised and regulated as a bank by the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) with its registered head office at Talstrasse 62, 8001 Zürich, Switzerland, and that its London Branch is authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority and subject to regulation by the Financial Conduct Authority and limited regulation by the Prudential Regulation Authority, FCA Firm Reference Number 487203. Buyer further represents that all such authorisations are in full force and effect, that it is not subject to any suspension, revocation, or restriction on any such authorisation that would materially affect its ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement, and that it is in compliance in all material respects with all applicable requirements of FINMA, the PRA, and the FCA. Buyer further represents that it maintains Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital in excess of the minimum requirements prescribed by FINMA and the PRA for its London Branch operations.
123: P122: Paragraph 10 — Events of Default
124: P123: Paragraph 10(a) — Standard Events of Default
125: P124: 10.1 Each of the following shall constitute an "Event of Default" with respect to a party (the "Defaulting Party"):
126: P125: (i) Failure to Pay or Deliver. Such party fails to pay any amount or deliver any Securities when due under this Agreement or any Transaction (including, without limitation, any Purchase Price, Repurchase Price, Cash Margin, Manufactured Payment, or margin transfer), and such failure continues for a period of one (1) Business Day after the Non-Defaulting Party gives written notice of such failure to the Defaulting Party. For the avoidance of doubt, "failure to pay" includes a failure to make a Manufactured Payment under Paragraph 5. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a failure caused solely by an administrative or operational error in a settlement system shall not constitute an Event of Default under this sub-paragraph (i) if such failure is cured within two (2) Business Days of the paying party becoming aware of such failure.
127: P126: (ii) Failure to Comply with Margin Call. Such party fails to comply with a Margin Call made in accordance with Paragraph 4 (including any failure to transfer Additional Purchased Securities, Equivalent Securities, or Cash Margin in the amount and by the time required), and such failure continues for a period of one (1) Business Day after the Non-Defaulting Party gives written notice of such failure to the Defaulting Party.
128: P127: (iii) Breach of Representation. Any representation or warranty made or deemed repeated by such party under Paragraph 9 (or elsewhere in this Agreement) is materially incorrect or misleading when made or when deemed repeated.
129: P128: (iv) Failure to Perform Other Obligations. Such party fails to perform any other material obligation under this Agreement and, if such failure is capable of remedy, such failure continues for thirty (30) calendar days after the Non-Defaulting Party gives written notice of such failure to the Defaulting Party specifying the nature of the failure and requiring its remedy.
130: P129: (v) Act of Insolvency. An Act of Insolvency occurs with respect to such party, as defined in the 2011 ICMA GMRA and as supplemented by Annex II, Section 11.
131: P130: (vi) Cross-Default. A Cross-Default occurs with respect to such party, as defined and supplemented by Annex II, Section 10.
132: P131: (vii) Material Adverse Change in Regulatory Status. A material adverse change in the regulatory status of such party occurs, including, without limitation, the suspension or revocation of such party's broker-dealer registration, banking licence, or authorisation to carry on regulated activities, or the imposition of any restriction on such party's regulated activities that would materially affect its ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
133: P132: Paragraph 10(b) — Consequences of an Event of Default
134: P133: 10.2 Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of an Event of Default with respect to a Defaulting Party, the Non-Defaulting Party may, at any time thereafter, by written notice to the Defaulting Party (or, in the case of an Act of Insolvency, without the requirement for any notice if the Act of Insolvency constitutes an ipso facto trigger as set out in Annex II, Section 11(b)), designate an "Early Termination Date" in respect of all (but not less than all) outstanding Transactions.
135: P134: 10.3 Upon designation of an Early Termination Date, no further payments or deliveries shall be required to be made by either party in respect of any Transaction, other than the net amount (if any) determined in accordance with the close-out and netting provisions of this Paragraph 10.
136: P135: 10.4 The standard close-out netting provisions of the 2011 ICMA GMRA shall apply. The Default Market Value of each Transaction shall be determined in accordance with Paragraph 10(d) of the 2011 ICMA GMRA, and the amounts so determined shall be aggregated and netted in accordance with the provisions thereof to produce a single net amount payable by one party to the other. The party owing such net amount shall pay it to the other party on the Early Termination Date (or, if such date is not a Business Day, on the next following Business Day) in the Base Currency.
137: P136: 10.5 The rights and remedies of the Non-Defaulting Party under this Paragraph 10 are in addition to, and without prejudice to, any other rights or remedies available to it under this Agreement, at law, or in equity.
138: P137: Paragraph 11 — Tax
139: P138: Paragraph 11(a) — General Tax Provisions
140: P139: 11.1 The standard tax provisions of the 2011 ICMA GMRA shall apply. Each party shall be responsible for its own tax obligations arising in connection with this Agreement and any Transaction, and each party shall provide to the other party such tax forms, certificates, and other documentation as the other party may reasonably request in order to establish any available exemption from, or reduction in the rate of, any withholding or deduction for or on account of tax.
141: P140: 11.2 Each party represents that it has provided, or will provide promptly upon request, accurate and complete information regarding its tax status, residency, and any applicable tax identification numbers to the other party, and will promptly notify the other party of any change in such information. Each party shall, upon request by the other party, deliver such tax forms and documentation (including IRS Forms W-8BEN-E or W-9, as applicable) as may be reasonably necessary to establish entitlement to any exemption from or reduction of withholding tax.
142: P141: Paragraph 11(b) — Tax Gross-Up
143: P142: 11.3 Elected. If either party (the "Tax Payor") is required by any applicable law, regulation, or governmental or regulatory authority to make any deduction or withholding from any payment due under this Agreement (including, without limitation, any Manufactured Payment, any payment of the Purchase Price or the Repurchase Price, any payment of Cash Margin, or any payment of a close-out amount), the Tax Payor shall pay such additional amounts (the "Tax Gross-Up Amounts") as may be necessary to ensure that the other party (the "Tax Payee") receives the full amount that it would have received had no such deduction or withholding been required.
144: P143: 11.4 The Tax Payor's obligation to pay Tax Gross-Up Amounts shall not apply to the extent that the deduction or withholding arises as a result of (a) the Tax Payee's failure to provide any tax form, certificate, or other documentation reasonably requested by the Tax Payor, (b) the Tax Payee's failure to comply with any applicable procedural requirement for claiming an exemption from or reduction in the rate of withholding, or (c) a change in tax residency of the Tax Payee after the date of this Agreement.
145: P144: 11.5 Cure Period. If a Tax Payor fails to pay any Tax Gross-Up Amount required under this Paragraph 11(b), the Tax Payee shall give written notice of such failure to the Tax Payor. The Tax Payor shall have a cure period of five (5) Business Days from receipt of such notice within which to pay the outstanding Tax Gross-Up Amount in full. Failure of the Tax Payor to cure such failure within such five (5) Business Day period shall constitute an Event of Default with respect to the Tax Payor, and the Tax Payee may thereafter exercise its rights under Paragraph 10(b) of this Agreement.
146: P145: Paragraph 12 — Interest
147: P146: 12.1 The standard interest provisions of the 2011 ICMA GMRA shall apply. If any amount payable by a party under this Agreement is not paid on the date on which it falls due, interest shall accrue on such unpaid amount from (and including) the due date to (but excluding) the date of actual payment, at a rate per annum equal to the overnight rate for the relevant currency (as determined by the Non-Defaulting Party in a commercially reasonable manner, by reference to the rate published by the relevant central bank or an equivalent interbank overnight rate source) plus one percent (1%) per annum. For the purposes of this Paragraph 12, the "overnight rate" for USD shall be the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York; for GBP, the Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) as published by the Bank of England; and for EUR, the Euro Short-Term Rate (€STR) as published by the European Central Bank.
148: P147: 12.2 Interest accruing under this Paragraph 12 shall be calculated on the basis of the actual number of days elapsed and a 360-day year (in the case of USD and EUR) or a 365-day year (in the case of GBP), and shall be payable on demand.
149: P148: 12.3 The payment of interest under this Paragraph 12 shall be without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to the Non-Defaulting Party under this Agreement or at law.
150: P149: Paragraph 13 — Single Agreement
151: P150: 13.1 This Agreement, Annex I, Annex II, and all Confirmations exchanged between the parties shall together constitute a single agreement between the parties. Each party acknowledges that it has entered into this Agreement, and will enter into each Transaction hereunder, in reliance on the fact that all such documents form a single agreement between the parties.
152: P151: 13.2 In the event of any inconsistency between the body of this Agreement and the terms of Annex I, Annex II, or any Confirmation, the order of priority set out in Paragraph 1.3 shall apply.
153: P152: Paragraph 14 — Notices
154: P153: 14.1 All notices, requests, demands, and other communications required or permitted to be given under this Agreement shall be in writing (which, for this purpose, includes electronic mail) and shall be delivered to the addresses and to the attention of the persons specified in Annex II, Section 14. Notices may be delivered by hand, by internationally recognised overnight courier, by facsimile (with confirmation of transmission), or by electronic mail to the email addresses specified in Annex II, Section 14.
155: P154: 14.2 Any such notice shall be deemed to be effective upon actual receipt by the addressee (or its authorised representative) at the address specified in Annex II, Section 14, or at such other address as the relevant party may have notified to the other party in writing in accordance with this Paragraph 14. For the purposes of this Paragraph 14, a notice shall be deemed received as follows: (a) if delivered by hand or internationally recognised overnight courier, on the date of delivery; (b) if delivered by facsimile or electronic mail, on the date of transmission, provided that if such transmission occurs after 5:00 p.m. in the recipient's time zone on a Business Day, or on a day that is not a Business Day, the notice shall be deemed received on the next following Business Day.
156: P155: 14.3 Either party may change its address, contact person, or electronic mail address for the purposes of this Paragraph 14 by giving not less than five (5) Business Days' prior written notice to the other party.
157: P156: Paragraph 15 — Entire Agreement; Severability
158: P157: 15.1 Entire Agreement. This Agreement (including Annex I, Annex II, and all Confirmations) constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, offers, discussions, and agreements (whether written or oral) between the parties relating to such subject matter.
159: P158: 15.2 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement (or any part thereof) is found by any court, tribunal, or arbitral body of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, unlawfulness, or unenforceability shall not affect the remaining provisions (or the remaining part of such provision) of this Agreement, which shall continue in full force and effect. The parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace any invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable provision with a valid and enforceable provision that, to the greatest extent possible, achieves the economic, commercial, and legal objectives of the invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable provision.
160: P159: 15.3 Amendments. No amendment or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by both parties.
161: P160: Paragraph 16 — Non-assignability; Termination
162: P161: 16.1 Non-assignability. Neither party may assign, transfer, charge, or otherwise dispose of any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party. Any purported assignment, transfer, charge, or disposal made in contravention of this Paragraph 16.1 shall be null and void and of no effect.
163: P162: 16.2 Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement (but not any outstanding Transaction) by giving not less than thirty (30) calendar days' prior written notice to the other party. Upon the effective date of such termination, no further Transactions may be entered into under this Agreement, but all Transactions outstanding at the effective date of termination shall continue to be governed by and subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement until all obligations of the parties in respect of such Transactions have been fully performed and discharged.
164: P163: Paragraph 17 — Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
165: P164: Paragraph 17(a) — Governing Law
166: P165: 17.1 This Agreement and any non-contractual obligations arising out of or in connection with it (including, without limitation, any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, and any claim based in tort, unjust enrichment, or any other legal or equitable principle) shall be governed by and construed in accordance with English law.
167: P166: 17.2 The choice of English law as the governing law of this Agreement shall not be affected by any change in the domicile, residence, registered office, or place of business of either party.
168: P167: Paragraph 17(b) — Dispute Resolution
169: P168: 17.3 Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of, relating to, or in connection with this Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, breach, or termination (a "Dispute"), shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration under the Rules of the London Court of International Arbitration ("LCIA") as in force at the time of filing of the request for arbitration (the "LCIA Rules"), which rules are deemed to be incorporated by reference into this Paragraph 17(b).
170: P169: 17.4 The seat, or legal place, of the arbitration shall be London, England. The designation of London as the seat of arbitration shall not preclude the holding of hearings, meetings, or deliberations at other locations if agreed by the parties or determined by the arbitral tribunal.
171: P170: 17.5 The number of arbitrators shall be three (3), unless the parties agree otherwise in writing after the Dispute has arisen. In the absence of any such agreement, (a) the claimant(s) shall nominate one arbitrator, (b) the respondent(s) shall nominate one arbitrator, and (c) the two arbitrators so nominated shall, within thirty (30) days of the nomination of the second arbitrator, agree upon and nominate a third arbitrator who shall serve as the presiding arbitrator. If the two party-nominated arbitrators fail to agree upon a presiding arbitrator within such thirty (30) day period, the LCIA Court shall appoint the presiding arbitrator in accordance with the LCIA Rules.
172: P171: 17.6 The language of the arbitration, including all written submissions, oral hearings, and the arbitral award, shall be English.
173: P172: 17.7 The arbitral award shall be final and binding on the parties, and judgment on the award may be entered and enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction, including (without limitation) any court of the State of New York, any court of the United States of America, and the courts of England and Wales. Each party irrevocably waives any right to challenge, resist, or oppose enforcement of such arbitral award in any jurisdiction.
174: P173: 17.8 Nothing in this Paragraph 17(b) shall prevent either party from seeking interim or conservatory measures from any court of competent jurisdiction, including injunctive relief, attachment, or other provisional remedies, and any such application shall not be deemed a waiver of, or inconsistent with, the agreement to arbitrate contained herein.
175: P174: 17.3 Each party irrevocably agrees that the courts of England and Wales shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of, relating to, or in connection with this Agreement (including any dispute regarding its existence, validity, or termination) (a "Dispute").
176: P175: 17.4 Each party irrevocably waives any objection to the laying of venue of any proceedings in such courts and any claim that such proceedings have been brought in an inconvenient forum.
177: P176: 17.5 Nothing in this Paragraph 17(b) shall limit the right of either party to take proceedings against the other party in any other court of competent jurisdiction, nor shall the taking of proceedings in any one or more jurisdictions preclude the taking of proceedings in any other jurisdiction, whether concurrently or not, to the extent permitted by applicable law.
178: P177: 17.6 For the avoidance of doubt, this clause confers non-exclusive, and not exclusive, jurisdiction.
179: P178: Paragraph 18 — No Waivers, etc.
180: P179: 18.1 No failure or delay by either party in exercising any right, power, or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right, power, or remedy preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power, or remedy.
181: P180: 18.2 No waiver of any provision of this Agreement or consent to any departure therefrom shall be effective unless given in writing and signed by the waiving party, and then such waiver or consent shall be effective only in the specific instance and for the specific purpose for which given.
182: P181: 18.3 The rights and remedies provided in this Agreement are cumulative and not exclusive of any rights or remedies provided by law.
183: P182: Paragraph 19 — Waiver of Immunity
184: P183: 19.1 Each party irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, with respect to itself and its revenues, assets, and properties (irrespective of their use or intended use), all immunity on the grounds of sovereignty or other similar grounds from (a) suit or proceeding, (b) jurisdiction of any court or tribunal, (c) relief by way of injunction or order for specific performance or recovery of property, (d) attachment of its assets (whether before or after judgment), and (e) execution or enforcement of any judgment, arbitral award, or order to which it or its revenues, assets, or properties might otherwise be entitled in any proceedings in the courts or tribunals of any jurisdiction.
185: P184: 19.2 Each party consents generally to the giving of any relief or the issue of any process in connection with any proceedings relating to this Agreement and any Transaction, and acknowledges that no immunity from such proceedings shall be claimed by or on behalf of itself or with respect to its assets.
186: P185: Paragraph 20 — Recording
187: P186: 20.1 Each party consents to the recording of telephone conversations and electronic communications (including, without limitation, electronic mail, instant messaging, and Bloomberg messaging) between the parties and between any persons acting on behalf of the parties in connection with this Agreement and any Transaction.
188: P187: 20.2 Each party acknowledges that such recordings may be used as evidence in any proceedings relating to this Agreement or any Transaction. Each party agrees to inform its relevant personnel that their communications may be recorded and to take such steps as may be necessary under applicable law to ensure that such recording is lawful. Each party waives any right to challenge the admissibility of such recordings in any proceedings arising out of or in connection with this Agreement on the grounds that such recordings were made without the consent of any person recorded.

191: P190: The full text of the Supplemental Terms and Conditions for the 2011 ICMA Global Master Repurchase Agreement, as published by the International Capital Market Association, is hereby incorporated by reference and forms part of this Agreement, without amendment except as expressly modified by Annex II (Elections, Supplements, and Amendments).

P55: Paragraph 4 — Margin Maintenance
P56: Paragraph 4(a) — Margin Deficit / Margin Excess

P57: 4.1 The parties shall, on each Business Day (or at such other intervals as may be agreed), mark to market all outstanding Transactions by reference to the Market Value of the Purchased Securities and the Transaction Exposure in respect of each Transaction, each calculated in the Base Currency.

P58: 4.2 If at any time the aggregate Cash Margin (if any) held by or on behalf of Buyer, together with the aggregate Market Value of all Purchased Securities held by Buyer (adjusted by the application of the relevant Haircut Percentage), is less than the aggregate Transaction Exposure of Buyer with respect to all Transactions then outstanding, a "Margin Deficit" shall be deemed to exist. The amount of such Margin Deficit shall be equal to the shortfall, calculated in the Base Currency.

P59: 4.3 If at any time the aggregate Market Value of all Purchased Securities held by Buyer (adjusted by the application of the relevant Haircut Percentage), together with any Cash Margin held by or on behalf of Buyer, exceeds the aggregate Transaction Exposure of Buyer with respect to all Transactions then outstanding, a "Margin Excess" shall be deemed to exist. The amount of such Margin Excess shall be equal to the surplus, calculated in the Base Currency.
P60: Paragraph 4(b) — Delivery Amount / Return Amount

P61: 4.4 Upon the existence of a Margin Deficit, Buyer may by notice to Seller (a "Margin Call") require Seller to transfer to Buyer Additional Purchased Securities or Cash Margin (or any combination thereof) in an amount sufficient to eliminate such Margin Deficit (the aggregate amount so required, the "Delivery Amount"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, no transfer shall be required if the Delivery Amount would be less than or equal to the applicable Margin Threshold specified in Annex II, Section 5(a) (being $250,000 $500,000 as of the date hereof).

P62: 4.5 Upon the existence of a Margin Excess, Seller may by notice to Buyer (also a "Margin Call") require Buyer to transfer to Seller Equivalent Securities or Cash Margin (or any combination thereof) sufficient to eliminate such Margin Excess (the aggregate amount so required, the "Return Amount"). Notwithstanding the foregoing, no transfer shall be required if the Return Amount would be less than or equal to the applicable Margin Threshold specified in Annex II, Section 5(b) (being $250,000 $500,000 as of the date hereof).

P63: 4.6 Any Additional Purchased Securities transferred by Seller to Buyer pursuant to a Margin Call must constitute Eligible Collateral, and the Market Value of such Additional Purchased Securities (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) shall be at least equal to the Delivery Amount.
P64: Paragraph 4(c) — Margin Call Timing

P65: 4.7 A Margin Call must be received by the other party by the margin call cut-off time specified in Annex II, Section 7 (being 10:00 a.m. London time as of the date hereof) in order for the resulting transfer to be required on that same Business Day.
P66: 4.8 If a Margin Call is received before the cut-off time on a Business Day, the party receiving the Margin Call shall make the required transfer on that same Business Day.

P67: 4.9 If a Margin Call is received at or after the cut-off time on a Business Day, or on a day that is not a Business Day, the party receiving the Margin Call shall make the required transfer on the next following Business Day.

P96: Paragraph 7 — Netting of Obligations
P97: Paragraph 7(a) — Payment Netting

P98: 7.1 The standard payment netting provisions of the 2011 ICMA GMRA shall apply. P122: Paragraph 10 — Events of Default
P123: Paragraph 10(a) — Standard Events of Default
P124: 10.1 Each of the following shall constitute an "Event of Default" with respect to a party (the "Defaulting Party"):

P125: (i) Failure to Pay or Deliver. Such party fails to pay any amount or deliver any Securities when due under this Agreement or any Transaction (including, without limitation, any Purchase Price, Repurchase Price, Cash Margin, Manufactured Payment, or margin transfer), and such failure continues for a period of one (1) Business Day after the Non-Defaulting Party gives written notice of such failure to the Defaulting Party. Notwithstanding the foregoing, a failure caused solely by an administrative or operational error in a settlement system shall not constitute an Event of Default under this sub-paragraph (i) if such failure is cured within two (2) Business Days of the paying party becoming aware of such failure.

P126: (ii) Failure to Comply with Margin Call. Such party fails to comply with a Margin Call made in accordance with Paragraph 4 (including any failure to transfer Additional Purchased Securities, Equivalent Securities, or Cash Margin in the amount and by the time required), and such failure continues for a period of one (1) Business Day after the Non-Defaulting Party gives written notice of such failure to the Defaulting Party.

P127: (iii) Breach of Representation. Any representation or warranty made or deemed repeated by such party under Paragraph 9 (or elsewhere in this Agreement) is materially incorrect or misleading when made or when deemed repeated.

P128: (iv) Failure to Perform Other Obligations. Such party fails to perform any other material obligation under this Agreement and, if such failure is capable of remedy, such failure continues for thirty (30) calendar days after the Non-Defaulting Party gives written notice of such failure to the Defaulting Party specifying the nature of the failure and requiring its remedy.
P129: (v) Act of Insolvency. An Act of Insolvency occurs with respect to such party, as defined in the 2011 ICMA GMRA and as supplemented by Annex II, Section 11.
P130: (vi) Cross-Default. A Cross-Default occurs with respect to such party, as defined and supplemented by Annex II, Section 10.

P131: (vii) Material Adverse Change in Regulatory Status. A material adverse change in the regulatory status of such party occurs, including, without limitation, the suspension or revocation of such party's broker-dealer registration, banking licence, or authorisation to carry on regulated activities, or the imposition of any restriction on such party's regulated activities that would materially affect its ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement.

P142: 11.3 Elected. If either party (the "Tax Payor") is required by any applicable law, regulation, or governmental or regulatory authority to make any deduction or withholding from any payment due under this Agreement (including, without limitation, any Manufactured Payment, any payment of the Purchase Price or the Repurchase Price, any payment of Cash Margin, or any payment of a close-out amount), the Tax Payor shall pay such additional amounts (the "Tax Gross-Up Amounts") as may be necessary to ensure that the other party (the "Tax Payee") receives the full amount that it would have received had no such deduction or withholding been required.

P143: 11.4 The Tax Payor's obligation to pay Tax Gross-Up Amounts shall not apply to the extent that the deduction or withholding arises as a result of (a) the Tax Payee's failure to provide any tax form, certificate, or other documentation reasonably requested by the Tax Payor, (b) the Tax Payee's failure to comply with any applicable procedural requirement for claiming an exemption from or reduction in the rate of withholding, or (c) a change in tax residency of the Tax Payee after the date of this Agreement.

P144: 11.5 Cure Period. If a Tax Payor fails to pay any Tax Gross-Up Amount required under this Paragraph 11(b), the Tax Payee shall give written notice of such failure to the Tax Payor. The Tax Payor shall have a cure period of five (5) Business Days from receipt of such notice within which to pay the outstanding Tax Gross-Up Amount in full. Failure of the Tax Payor to cure such failure within such five (5) Business Day period shall constitute an Event of Default with respect to the Tax Payor, and the Tax Payee may thereafter exercise its rights under Paragraph 10(b) of this Agreement.
P145: Paragraph 12 — Interest

P146: 12.1 The standard interest provisions of the 2011 ICMA GMRA shall apply. If any amount payable by a party under this Agreement is not paid on the date on which it falls due, interest shall accrue on such unpaid amount from (and including) the due date to (but excluding) the date of actual payment, at a rate per annum equal to the overnight rate for the relevant currency (as determined by the Non-Defaulting Party in a commercially reasonable manner, by reference to the rate published by the relevant central bank or an equivalent interbank overnight rate source) plus one percent (1%) per annum. For the purposes of this Paragraph 12, the "overnight rate" for USD shall be the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York; for GBP, the Sterling Overnight Index Average (SONIA) as published by the Bank of England; and for EUR, the Euro Short-Term Rate (€STR) as published by the European Central Bank.

P147: 12.2 Interest accruing under this Paragraph 12 shall be calculated on the basis of the actual number of days elapsed and a 360-day year (in the case of USD and EUR) or a 365-day year (in the case of GBP), and shall be payable on demand.
P148: 12.3 The payment of interest under this Paragraph 12 shall be without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to the Non-Defaulting Party under this Agreement or at law.
P149: Paragraph 13 — Single Agreement

P150: 13.1 This Agreement, Annex I, Annex II, and all Confirmations exchanged between the parties shall together constitute a single agreement between the parties. Each party acknowledges that it has entered into this Agreement, and will enter into each Transaction hereunder, in reliance on the fact that all such documents form a single agreement between the parties.
P151: 13.2 In the event of any inconsistency between the body of this Agreement and the terms of Annex I, Annex II, or any Confirmation, the order of priority set out in Paragraph 1.3 shall apply.
P152: Paragraph 14 — Notices

P153: 14.1 All notices, requests, demands, and other communications required or permitted to be given under this Agreement shall be in writing (which, for this purpose, includes electronic mail) and shall be delivered to the addresses and to the attention of the persons specified in Annex II, Section 14. Notices may be delivered by hand, by internationally recognised overnight courier, by facsimile (with confirmation of transmission), or by electronic mail to the email addresses specified in Annex II, Section 14.

P154: 14.2 Any such notice shall be deemed to be effective upon actual receipt by the addressee (or its authorised representative) at the address specified in Annex II, Section 14, or at such other address as the relevant party may have notified to the other party in writing in accordance with this Paragraph 14. For the purposes of this Paragraph 14, a notice shall be deemed received as follows: (a) if delivered by hand or internationally recognised overnight courier, on the date of delivery; (b) if delivered by facsimile or electronic mail, on the date of transmission, provided that if such transmission occurs after 5:00 p.m. in the recipient's time zone on a Business Day, or on a day that is not a Business Day, the notice shall be deemed received on the next following Business Day.

P155: 14.3 Either party may change its address, contact person, or electronic mail address for the purposes of this Paragraph 14 by giving not less than five (5) Business Days' prior written notice to the other party.
P156: Paragraph 15 — Entire Agreement; Severability

P157: 15.1 Entire Agreement. This Agreement (including Annex I, Annex II, and all Confirmations) constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, offers, discussions, and agreements (whether written or oral) between the parties relating to such subject matter.

P158: 15.2 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement (or any part thereof) is found by any court, tribunal, or arbitral body of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, unlawfulness, or unenforceability shall not affect the remaining provisions (or the remaining part of such provision) of this Agreement, which shall continue in full force and effect. The parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace any invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable provision with a valid and enforceable provision that, to the greatest extent possible, achieves the economic, commercial, and legal objectives of the invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable provision.
P159: 15.3 Amendments. No amendment or waiver of any provision of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by both parties.
P160: Paragraph 16 — Non-assignability; Termination

P161: 16.1 Non-assignability. Neither party may assign, transfer, charge, or otherwise dispose of any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party. Any purported assignment, transfer, charge, or disposal made in contravention of this Paragraph 16.1 shall be null and void and of no effect.

P162: 16.2 Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement (but not any outstanding Transaction) by giving not less than thirty (30) calendar days' prior written notice to the other party. Upon the effective date of such termination, no further Transactions may be entered into under this Agreement, but all Transactions outstanding at the effective date of termination shall continue to be governed by and subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement until all obligations of the parties in respect of such Transactions have been fully performed and discharged.
P163: Paragraph 17 — Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
P164: Paragraph 17(a) — Governing Law

P165: 17.1 This Agreement and any non-contractual obligations arising out of or in connection with it (including, without limitation, any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, and any claim based in tort, unjust enrichment, or any other legal or equitable principle) shall be governed by and construed in accordance with English law.
P166: 17.2 The choice of English law as the governing law of this Agreement shall not be affected by any change in the domicile, residence, registered office, or place of business of either party.
P167: Paragraph 17(b) — Dispute Resolution

P168: 17.3 Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of, relating to, or in connection with this Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, breach, or termination (a "Dispute"), shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration under the Rules of the London Court of International Arbitration ("LCIA") as in force at the time of filing of the request for arbitration (the "LCIA Rules"), which rules are deemed to be incorporated by reference into this Paragraph 17(b).

P169: 17.4 The seat, or legal place, of the arbitration shall be London, England. The designation of London as the seat of arbitration shall not preclude the holding of hearings, meetings, or deliberations at other locations if agreed by the parties or determined by the arbitral tribunal.

P170: 17.5 The number of arbitrators shall be three (3), unless the parties agree otherwise in writing after the Dispute has arisen. In the absence of any such agreement, (a) the claimant(s) shall nominate one arbitrator, (b) the respondent(s) shall nominate one arbitrator, and (c) the two arbitrators so nominated shall, within thirty (30) days of the nomination of the second arbitrator, agree upon and nominate a third arbitrator who shall serve as the presiding arbitrator. If the two party-nominated arbitrators fail to agree upon a presiding arbitrator within such thirty (30) day period, the LCIA Court shall appoint the presiding arbitrator in accordance with the LCIA Rules.
P171: 17.6 The language of the arbitration, including all written submissions, oral hearings, and the arbitral award, shall be English.

P172: 17.7 The arbitral award shall be final and binding on the parties, and judgment on the award may be entered and enforced in any court of competent jurisdiction, including (without limitation) any court of the State of New York, any court of the United States of America, and the courts of England and Wales. Each party irrevocably waives any right to challenge, resist, or oppose enforcement of such arbitral award in any jurisdiction.

P173: 17.8 Nothing in this Paragraph 17(b) shall prevent either party from seeking interim or conservatory measures from any court of competent jurisdiction, including injunctive relief, attachment, or other provisional remedies, and any such application shall not be deemed a waiver of, or inconsistent with, the agreement to arbitrate contained herein.

P174: 17.3 Each party irrevocably agrees that the courts of England and Wales shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of, relating to, or in connection with this Agreement (including any dispute regarding its existence, validity, or termination) (a "Dispute").
P175: 17.4 Each party irrevocably waives any objection to the laying of venue of any proceedings in such courts and any claim that such proceedings have been brought in an inconvenient forum.

P176: 17.5 Nothing in this Paragraph 17(b) shall limit the right of either party to take proceedings against the other party in any other court of competent jurisdiction, nor shall the taking of proceedings in any one or more jurisdictions preclude the taking of proceedings in any other jurisdiction, whether concurrently or not, to the extent permitted by applicable law.
P177: 17.6 For the avoidance of doubt, this clause confers non-exclusive, and not exclusive, jurisdiction.
P178: Paragraph 18 — No Waivers, etc.

P179: 18.1 No failure or delay by either party in exercising any right, power, or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right, power, or remedy preclude any other or further exercise thereof or the exercise of any other right, power, or remedy.

P180: 18.2 No waiver of any provision of this Agreement or consent to any departure therefrom shall be effective unless given in writing and signed by the waiving party, and then such waiver or consent shall be effective only in the specific instance and for the specific purpose for which given.
P181: 18.3 The rights and remedies provided in this Agreement are cumulative and not exclusive of any rights or remedies provided by law.
P182: Paragraph 19 — Waiver of Immunity

P183: 19.1 Each party irrevocably waives, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, with respect to itself and its revenues, assets, and properties (irrespective of their use or intended use), all immunity on the grounds of sovereignty or other similar grounds from (a) suit or proceeding, (b) jurisdiction of any court or tribunal, (c) relief by way of injunction or order for specific performance or recovery of property, (d) attachment of its assets (whether before or after judgment), and (e) execution or enforcement of any judgment, arbitral award, or order to which it or its revenues, assets, or properties might otherwise be entitled in any proceedings in the courts or tribunals of any jurisdiction.

P184: 19.2 Each party consents generally to the giving of any relief or the issue of any process in connection with any proceedings relating to this Agreement and any Transaction, and acknowledges that no immunity from such proceedings shall be claimed by or on behalf of itself or with respect to its assets.
P185: Paragraph 20 — Recording

P186: 20.1 Each party consents to the recording of telephone conversations and electronic communications (including, without limitation, electronic mail, instant messaging, and Bloomberg messaging) between the parties and between any persons acting on behalf of the parties in connection with this Agreement and any Transaction.

P187: 20.2 Each party acknowledges that such recordings may be used as evidence in any proceedings relating to this Agreement or any Transaction. Each party agrees to inform its relevant personnel that their communications may be recorded and to take such steps as may be necessary under applicable law to ensure that such recording is lawful. Each party waives any right to challenge the admissibility of such recordings in any proceedings arising out of or in connection with this Agreement on the grounds that such recordings were made without the consent of any person recorded.

190: P189: ANNEX I — SUPPLEMENTAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS (2011 Version)
191: P190: The full text of the Supplemental Terms and Conditions for the 2011 ICMA Global Master Repurchase Agreement, as published by the International Capital Market Association, is hereby incorporated by reference and forms part of this Agreement, without amendment except as expressly modified by Annex II (Elections, Supplements, and Amendments).
192: P191: The 2011 Annex I sets out the standard supplemental terms governing, among other matters:
193: P192: (a) additional margin maintenance provisions, including the calculation of Transaction Exposure, the valuation methodology for determining Market Value, and the treatment of accrued but unpaid Income;
194: P193: (b) default valuation provisions, including the methodology for determining the Default Market Value of Purchased Securities and Equivalent Securities upon the occurrence of an Event of Default and the designation of an Early Termination Date;
195: P194: (c) mini close-out provisions, including the right of the Non-Defaulting Party to close out individual Transactions following the occurrence and continuance of an Event of Default, without prejudice to its right to designate an Early Termination Date in respect of all outstanding Transactions;
196: P195: (d) provisions relating to the treatment of margin transfers, the application of Cash Margin, and the right to apply equivalent margin in the form of Additional Purchased Securities;
197: P196: (e) provisions relating to the acceleration and termination of Transactions upon the occurrence of specified events; and
198: P197: (f) such other supplemental terms and conditions as form part of the standard 2011 ICMA GMRA framework.
199: P198: The parties acknowledge and agree that the provisions of the 2011 Annex I are an integral part of this Agreement and shall be read and construed together with the body of this Agreement and Annex II. In the event of any inconsistency between the provisions of the 2011 Annex I and the provisions of Annex II, the provisions of Annex II shall prevail.

201: P200: ANNEX II — ELECTIONS, SUPPLEMENTS, AND AMENDMENTS
202: P201: Section 1 — Parties

213: P212: Full legal name: Meridian Capital Securities LLC

221: P220: Section 2 — Base Currency
222: P221: The Base Currency for all purposes under this Agreement shall be United States Dollars (USD). All calculations required to be made under this Agreement in a single currency (including calculations of Transaction Exposure, Margin Deficit, Margin Excess, Net Exposure, Delivery Amount, Return Amount, and Default Market Value) shall be made in, or converted into, the Base Currency at the spot rate of exchange prevailing at the relevant time of determination, as reasonably determined by Buyer.
223: P222: Section 3 — Eligible Collateral
224: P223: (a) "Eligible Sovereign Securities" means fixed-rate or floating-rate debt securities denominated in USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, or CHF and issued by the central government (or a central government-guaranteed agency) of any of the following G7 nations: the United States of America, the United Kingdom, Germany (Bundesrepublik Deutschland), France (République française), Japan, Canada, and Italy (Repubblica Italiana), provided that:
225: P224: (i) such securities have a long-term issuer credit rating of not less than A– by S&P Global Ratings ("S&P") or A3 by Moody's Investors Service ("Moody's") (or, if rated by both, meeting at least one such threshold at the relevant time of determination);
226: P225: (ii) such securities are eligible for settlement through Clearstream Banking S.A. (in the case of Euro-denominated securities) or The Depository Trust Company (in the case of USD-denominated securities); and
227: P226: (iii) such securities are not subject to any lien, charge, pledge, encumbrance, or other security interest (other than any arising under this Agreement or the applicable settlement system rules).
228: P227: (b) "Eligible Corporate Securities" means fixed-rate or floating-rate debt securities issued by a corporate issuer (including, for the avoidance of doubt, securities issued by a corporate entity that is not a sovereign or government-guaranteed entity), provided that:
229: P228: (i) such securities have a long-term issuer credit rating of not less than BBB+ by S&P or Baa1 by Moody's (or, if rated by both, meeting at least one such threshold at the relevant time of determination);
230: P229: (ii) the residual maturity of such securities does not exceed ten (10) years from the relevant Purchase Date;
231: P230: (iii) such securities are eligible for settlement through Clearstream Banking S.A. (in the case of Euro-denominated securities) or The Depository Trust Company (in the case of USD-denominated securities);
232: P231: (iv) such securities are not convertible, exchangeable, or equity-linked;
233: P232: (v) such securities are not subordinated obligations of the issuer; and
234: P233: (vi) such securities are not subject to any lien, charge, pledge, encumbrance, or other security interest (other than any arising under this Agreement or the applicable settlement system rules).
235: P234: (c) "Eligible Collateral" means Eligible Sovereign Securities and Eligible Corporate Securities, collectively.
236: P235: (d) Buyer reserves the right, in its sole and reasonable discretion, to refuse to accept any securities proposed by Seller as Purchased Securities or Additional Purchased Securities if, in Buyer's reasonable opinion, such securities do not satisfy the eligibility criteria set out in this Section 3 or if market conditions or credit considerations so warrant. Any such refusal shall be communicated to Seller promptly in writing.
237: P236: Section 4 — Haircuts
238: P237: (a) Eligible Sovereign Securities:
239: P238: Haircut Percentage: 2.0% 1.5% (the "Sovereign Haircut").
240: P239: Application: The Purchase Price for a Transaction in which the Purchased Securities are Eligible Sovereign Securities shall be determined by dividing the Market Value of such Purchased Securities (as of the relevant Purchase Date or, in the case of Additional Purchased Securities, as of the date of transfer) by 1.020 1.015.
241: P240: Illustrative example: If the Market Value of Eligible Sovereign Securities is $100,000,000, the Purchase Price shall be $100,000,000 ÷ 1.020 = $98,039,215.69 1.015 = $98,522,167.49.
242: P241: (b) Eligible Corporate Securities:
243: P242: Haircut Percentage: 5.0% 3.5% (the "Corporate Haircut").
244: P243: Application: The Purchase Price for a Transaction in which the Purchased Securities are Eligible Corporate Securities shall be determined by dividing the Market Value of such Purchased Securities (as of the relevant Purchase Date or, in the case of Additional Purchased Securities, as of the date of transfer) by 1.050 1.035.
245: P244: Illustrative example: If the Market Value of Eligible Corporate Securities is $50,000,000, the Purchase Price shall be $50,000,000 ÷ 1.050 = $47,619,047.62 1.035 = $48,309,178.74.
246: P245: (c) The Haircut Percentages set out in this Section 4 shall apply to the initial pricing of each Transaction and to the valuation of Purchased Securities and Additional Purchased Securities for the purposes of Paragraph 4 (Margin Maintenance). For the avoidance of doubt, the Haircut Percentage applicable to a Transaction shall be determined by reference to the category of Eligible Collateral into which the relevant Purchased Securities fall at the time of the initial Transaction and shall not change during the life of that Transaction unless the Purchased Securities are substituted in accordance with Paragraph 8 and Annex II, Section 9, in which case the Haircut Percentage applicable to the Alternative Securities shall apply from the date of substitution.
247: P246: Section 5 — Margin Thresholds
248: P247: (a) Delivery Amount (Margin Deficit — payable by Seller):
249: P248: Margin Threshold: $250,000 (two hundred fifty thousand United States Dollars) $500,000 (five hundred thousand United States Dollars).
250: P249: No obligation to deliver Additional Purchased Securities or Cash Margin arises unless the Delivery Amount (calculated in the Base Currency on an aggregate net basis across all outstanding Transactions) exceeds $250,000 $500,000.
251: P250: (b) Return Amount (Margin Excess — payable by Buyer):
252: P251: Margin Threshold: $250,000 (two hundred fifty thousand United States Dollars) $500,000 (five hundred thousand United States Dollars).
253: P252: No obligation to return Equivalent Securities or Cash Margin arises unless the Return Amount (calculated in the Base Currency on an aggregate net basis across all outstanding Transactions) exceeds $250,000 $500,000.
254: P253: (c) The Margin Thresholds set forth in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) above apply on an aggregate net basis across all outstanding Transactions. For the avoidance of doubt, the Margin Threshold is not applied on a per-Transaction basis; rather, the aggregate Delivery Amount or Return Amount across all Transactions must exceed the applicable Margin Threshold before any transfer obligation arises.
255: P254: Section 6 — Net Exposure Cap
256: P255: 6.1 The aggregate net exposure of Buyer to Seller under all Transactions outstanding at any time shall not exceed $1,500,000,000 (one billion five hundred million United States Dollars) (the "Net Exposure Cap").
257: P256: 6.2 For the purposes of this Section 6, "net exposure" means the aggregate Transaction Exposure of all outstanding Transactions (after application of the relevant Haircuts and after deduction of any Cash Margin held by or on behalf of Buyer), calculated in the Base Currency as of the most recent mark-to-market determination.
258: P257: 6.3 If at any time the net exposure would exceed the Net Exposure Cap (whether as a result of a proposed new Transaction, a decline in the Market Value of Purchased Securities, or otherwise), Buyer shall not be required to enter into any further Transaction and Seller shall, promptly upon notice from Buyer, deliver additional Eligible Collateral or cash in an amount sufficient to reduce the net exposure below the Net Exposure Cap. Failure by Seller to make such delivery within one (1) Business Day of receipt of such notice shall constitute a failure to comply with a Margin Call for the purposes of Paragraph 10(a)(ii).
259: P258: 6.4 The Net Exposure Cap may be amended from time to time by mutual written agreement of the parties.
260: P259: Section 7 — Margin Call Cut-off Time and Settlement
261: P260: (a) The margin call cut-off time shall be 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day.
262: P261: (b) If a Margin Call is given and received before 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day, the resulting transfer of Additional Purchased Securities, Equivalent Securities, or Cash Margin (as applicable) shall be effected on that same Business Day.
263: P262: (c) If a Margin Call is given or received at or after 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day, or on a day that is not a Business Day, the resulting transfer shall be effected on the next following Business Day.
264: P263: (d) For the purposes of this Section 7, a Margin Call shall be deemed to have been "received" at the time of actual receipt by the addressee at the notice details specified in Section 14 of this Annex II. Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to and acknowledge receipt of a Margin Call promptly upon receipt.
265: P264: Section 8 — Netting
266: P265: Paragraph 7(b) of the Agreement (settlement netting for obligations in the same currency falling due on the same settlement date) is elected and applicable. Accordingly, where on any Business Day amounts would otherwise be payable in the same currency and on the same settlement date by each party to the other under this Agreement, such amounts shall be netted in accordance with Paragraph 7(b) of the Agreement, and only the resulting net amount shall be payable by the party owing such amount.
267: P266: Section 9 — Substitution
268: P267: (a) Seller may, from time to time during the term of any Transaction, request the effect a substitution of Alternative Securities for all or any part of the Purchased Securities in that Transaction. Any such request notice shall be made in writing (including by electronic mail) and shall specify in reasonable detail the Purchased Securities to be replaced, the proposed Alternative Securities (including ISIN, nominal amount, issuer, coupon, maturity, and credit rating), and the proposed substitution date.
269: P268: (b) Any such substitution shall require the prior written consent of Buyer. Buyer may grant, withhold, condition, or delay such consent in its sole and absolute discretion and shall not be required to provide any reason for any refusal. Buyer shall use reasonable efforts to respond to any request for substitution within two (2) Business Days of receipt, but any failure to respond within such period shall not constitute consent.
270: P269: (b) Seller shall give Buyer not less than one (1) Business Day's prior notice of any proposed substitution. No consent of Buyer shall be required.
271: P270: (c) Where Buyer consents, the a substitution shall be is effected on the Business Day agreed by the parties (or, failing agreement, on the second Business Day following Buyer's consent) on the Business Day specified in Seller's notice, by simultaneous transfer of the Alternative Securities to Buyer (or to Buyer's account at the relevant settlement system) and the Purchased Securities to Seller (or to Seller's account at the relevant settlement system), through the applicable settlement system in accordance with Paragraph 6.
272: P271: (d) Alternative Securities must qualify as Eligible Collateral and must satisfy all of the eligibility criteria set out in Section 3 of this Annex II. The Market Value of the Alternative Securities (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) must be at least equal to the Market Value of the Purchased Securities being replaced (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) as of the close of business on the Business Day immediately preceding the substitution date. If the Alternative Securities fall into a different category of Eligible Collateral than the Purchased Securities being replaced, the Haircut Percentage applicable to the Alternative Securities shall apply from the date of substitution.
273: P272: (e) Upon completion of a substitution, the Alternative Securities shall become the Purchased Securities for all purposes of the relevant Transaction, and the Confirmation for such Transaction shall be deemed to have been amended accordingly. For the avoidance of doubt, the occurrence of a substitution shall not affect the Purchase Date, the Repurchase Date, or the Pricing Rate of the relevant Transaction, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
274: P273: Section 10 — Cross-Default
275: P274: (a) For the purposes of Paragraph 10(a)(vi) of the Agreement, a "Cross-Default" shall occur with respect to a party if:
276: P275: (i) such party fails to make any payment or delivery when due (after giving effect to any applicable grace period) under one or more agreements or instruments relating to Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold; or
277: P276: (ii) such party's Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold is accelerated, or becomes capable of being accelerated, prior to its stated maturity as a result of a default (howsoever described) thereunder; or
278: P277: (iii) any security interest securing Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold becomes enforceable and is enforced (including by the taking of possession or the appointment of a receiver, administrative receiver, manager, or other similar officer).
279: P278: (b) "Specified Indebtedness" means any obligation (whether present or future, contingent or otherwise, as principal or surety or otherwise) in respect of borrowed money. For the avoidance of doubt, Specified Indebtedness includes obligations under loan agreements, credit facilities, overdraft facilities, note purchase agreements, bond indentures, guarantees of borrowed money, and similar instruments, but excludes obligations under this Agreement and under any other agreement that is a GMRA, GMSLA, or ISDA Master Agreement between the parties.
280: P279: (c) "Cross-Default Threshold" means, with respect to each party, $10,000,000 (ten million United States Dollars) $50,000,000 (fifty million United States Dollars) (or its equivalent in any other currency, converted into the Base Currency at the spot rate of exchange at the relevant time).
281: P280: (d) For the purposes of determining whether the Cross-Default Threshold has been exceeded, all amounts of Specified Indebtedness in respect of which the relevant event has occurred shall be aggregated (regardless of whether such amounts arise under the same or different agreements or instruments).
282: P281: Section 11 — Act of Insolvency
283: P282: (a) The definition of "Act of Insolvency" shall be as set out in the 2011 ICMA GMRA, supplemented as follows.
284: P283: (b) Grace Period: None (zero days). An Act of Insolvency shall constitute an Event of Default immediately and automatically upon occurrence, without requirement for notice or lapse of any period of time (an "ipso facto trigger"). For the avoidance of doubt, upon the occurrence of an Act of Insolvency with respect to a party, the other party shall be entitled, without the requirement for any notice to the Defaulting Party, to designate an Early Termination Date in respect of all outstanding Transactions in accordance with Paragraph 10(b). Grace Period: Thirty (30) calendar days. An Act of Insolvency shall not constitute an Event of Default unless it has continued unremedied for a period of thirty (30) calendar days following the date on which the Non-Defaulting Party first becomes aware of, or receives written notice of, such Act of Insolvency (the "Act of Insolvency Grace Period").
285: P284: (c) For the avoidance of doubt, and without limiting the definition of Act of Insolvency set out in the 2011 ICMA GMRA, each of the following shall constitute an Act of Insolvency for the purposes of this Agreement:
286: P285: (i) the appointment of a receiver, administrator, liquidator, conservator, trustee, custodian, or similar official over a party or any material part of its assets, whether by a court of competent jurisdiction, a governmental or regulatory authority, or otherwise;
287: P286: (ii) the filing of any petition, application, or proceeding (whether voluntary or involuntary) seeking any such appointment or seeking any arrangement, reorganisation, composition, readjustment, liquidation, dissolution, winding-up, or similar relief under any applicable insolvency, bankruptcy, receivership, administration, or similar law;
288: P287: (iii) the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors;
289: P288: (iv) the admission in writing by a party of its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due;
290: P289: (v) the taking of any corporate or other action by a party in furtherance of any of the foregoing; or
291: P290: (vi) any analogous event or proceeding in any jurisdiction.
292: P291: Section 12 — Repricing / Mini Close-out

Such repricing (a "Repricing Event") may be exercised on the 90th calendar day following the Purchase Date of the relevant Transaction, or on the anniversary of any prior Repricing Date if the Transaction remains outstanding (each such date, a "Repricing Date"). 294: P293: (b) Buyer shall exercise a Repricing Event by delivering written notice to Seller not less than two (2) Business Days prior to the applicable Repricing Date. Such notice shall specify the Transaction to be repriced and the proposed Repricing Date.
295: P294: (c) Upon the occurrence of a Repricing Event:
296: P295: (i) the original Transaction shall terminate on the Repricing Date as if such date were the Repurchase Date, and Seller shall pay to Buyer the Repurchase Price applicable to the original Transaction as of the Repricing Date;
297: P296: (ii) simultaneously, the parties shall enter into a new Transaction on terms identical to the original Transaction, save that:
298: P297: (A) the Purchase Date of the new Transaction shall be the Repricing Date;
299: P298: (B) the Purchase Price of the new Transaction shall be recalculated based on the Market Value of the Purchased Securities on the Repricing Date (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage); and

301: P300: (iii) the close-out amount, if any, arising from the termination of the original Transaction and the simultaneous commencement of the new Transaction shall be calculated as the difference between the Repurchase Price of the original Transaction and the Purchase Price of the new Transaction. Such close-out amount shall be settled in cash on the Repricing Date by the party owing the net amount to the other party.
302: P301: (d) The repricing mechanic set out in this Section 12 does not affect either party's rights under Paragraph 4 (Margin Maintenance) or Paragraph 10 (Events of Default). For the avoidance of doubt, the existence of a Repricing Event or the exercise of a Repricing Event shall not relieve either party of its obligations to make margin transfers or to comply with Margin Calls during the period between the date of notice and the Repricing Date.
303: P302: (e) The parties acknowledge that the purpose of the repricing mechanic is to adjust the economic terms of outstanding Transactions to reflect current market conditions and to manage the credit exposure of the parties. The new Transaction entered into on a Repricing Date shall, for all purposes of this Agreement, be treated as a new and separate Transaction.
304: P303: (a) No repricing or mini close-out of any Transaction shall occur during the term of such Transaction. Repricing shall take place only upon the scheduled maturity of a Transaction, at which time the parties may, by mutual agreement, enter into a new Transaction at a Purchase Price recalculated based on the then-current Market Value of the Purchased Securities (after application of the relevant Haircut).
305: P304: (b) For the avoidance of doubt, neither party shall have any right to require a repricing, reset, or mini close-out of any Transaction prior to its scheduled Repurchase Date, and the margin maintenance provisions of Paragraph 4 of this Agreement shall be the sole mechanism for addressing changes in the Market Value of Purchased Securities during the term of a Transaction.
306: P305: (c) Nothing in this Section 12 shall affect either party's rights under Paragraph 10 (Events of Default).
307: P306: Section 13 — Tax Gross-Up
