lines.text: P189: ANNEX I — SUPPLEMENTAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS (2011 Version)

P190: The full text of the Supplemental Terms and Conditions for the 2011 ICMA Global Master Repurchase Agreement, as published by the International Capital Market Association, is hereby incorporated by reference and forms part of this Agreement, without amendment except as expressly modified by Annex II (Elections, Supplements, and Amendments).
P191: The 2011 Annex I sets out the standard supplemental terms governing, among other matters:

P192: (a) additional margin maintenance provisions, including the calculation of Transaction Exposure, the valuation methodology for determining Market Value, and the treatment of accrued but unpaid Income;

P193: (b) default valuation provisions, including the methodology for determining the Default Market Value of Purchased Securities and Equivalent Securities upon the occurrence of an Event of Default and the designation of an Early Termination Date;

P194: (c) mini close-out provisions, including the right of the Non-Defaulting Party to close out individual Transactions following the occurrence and continuance of an Event of Default, without prejudice to its right to designate an Early Termination Date in respect of all outstanding Transactions;
P195: (d) provisions relating to the treatment of margin transfers, the application of Cash Margin, and the right to apply equivalent margin in the form of Additional Purchased Securities;
P196: (e) provisions relating to the acceleration and termination of Transactions upon the occurrence of specified events; and
P197: (f) such other supplemental terms and conditions as form part of the standard 2011 ICMA GMRA framework.

P198: The parties acknowledge and agree that the provisions of the 2011 Annex I are an integral part of this Agreement and shall be read and construed together with the body of this Agreement and Annex II. In the event of any inconsistency between the provisions of the 2011 Annex I and the provisions of Annex II, the provisions of Annex II shall prevail.
P200: ANNEX II — ELECTIONS, SUPPLEMENTS, AND AMENDMENTS
P201: Section 1 — Parties
P202: (a) Buyer:
P203: Full legal name: Voss Bank AG, acting through its London Branch
P204: Registered head office: Talstrasse 62, 8001 Zürich, Switzerland

P211: (b) Seller:
P212: Full legal name: Meridian Capital Securities LLC
P213: Principal office: 200 Vesey Street, 38th Floor, New York, NY 10281, USA
P214: Registered agent: Corporation Service Company, 251 Little Falls Drive, Wilmington, DE 19808, USA

P219: Regulators: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission; Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA)
P220: Section 2 — Base Currency

P221: The Base Currency for all purposes under this Agreement shall be United States Dollars (USD). All calculations required to be made under this Agreement in a single currency (including calculations of Transaction Exposure, Margin Deficit, Margin Excess, Net Exposure, Delivery Amount, Return Amount, and Default Market Value) shall be made in, or converted into, the Base Currency at the spot rate of exchange prevailing at the relevant time of determination, as reasonably determined by Buyer.
P222: Section 3 — Eligible Collateral

P223: (a) "Eligible Sovereign Securities" means fixed-rate or floating-rate debt securities denominated in USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CAD, or CHF and issued by the central government (or a central government-guaranteed agency) of any of the following G7 nations: the United States of America, the United Kingdom, Germany (Bundesrepublik Deutschland), France (République française), Japan, Canada, and Italy (Repubblica Italiana), provided that:

P224: (i) such securities have a long-term issuer credit rating of not less than A– by S&P Global Ratings ("S&P") or A3 by Moody's Investors Service ("Moody's") (or, if rated by both, meeting at least one such threshold at the relevant time of determination);

P225: (ii) such securities are eligible for settlement through Clearstream Banking S.A. (in the case of Euro-denominated securities) or The Depository Trust Company (in the case of USD-denominated securities); and

P226: (iii) such securities are not subject to any lien, charge, pledge, encumbrance, or other security interest (other than any arising under this Agreement or the applicable settlement system rules).

P227: (b) "Eligible Corporate Securities" means fixed-rate or floating-rate debt securities issued by a corporate issuer (including, for the avoidance of doubt, securities issued by a corporate entity that is not a sovereign or government-guaranteed entity), provided that:

P228: (i) such securities have a long-term issuer credit rating of not less than BBB+ by S&P or Baa1 by Moody's (or, if rated by both, meeting at least one such threshold at the relevant time of determination);
P229: (ii) the residual maturity of such securities does not exceed ten (10) years from the relevant Purchase Date;

P230: (iii) such securities are eligible for settlement through Clearstream Banking S.A. (in the case of Euro-denominated securities) or The Depository Trust Company (in the case of USD-denominated securities);
P231: (iv) such securities are not convertible, exchangeable, or equity-linked;
P232: (v) such securities are not subordinated obligations of the issuer; and

P233: (vi) such securities are not subject to any lien, charge, pledge, encumbrance, or other security interest (other than any arising under this Agreement or the applicable settlement system rules).
P234: (c) "Eligible Collateral" means Eligible Sovereign Securities and Eligible Corporate Securities, collectively.

P235: (d) Buyer reserves the right, in its sole and reasonable discretion, to refuse to accept any securities proposed by Seller as Purchased Securities or Additional Purchased Securities if, in Buyer's reasonable opinion, such securities do not satisfy the eligibility criteria set out in this Section 3 or if market conditions or credit considerations so warrant. Any such refusal shall be communicated to Seller promptly in writing.
P236: Section 4 — Haircuts
P237: (a) Eligible Sovereign Securities:
P238: Haircut Percentage: 2.0% 1.5% (the "Sovereign Haircut").

P239: Application: The Purchase Price for a Transaction in which the Purchased Securities are Eligible Sovereign Securities shall be determined by dividing the Market Value of such Purchased Securities (as of the relevant Purchase Date or, in the case of Additional Purchased Securities, as of the date of transfer) by 1.020 1.015.
P240: Illustrative example: If the Market Value of Eligible Sovereign Securities is $100,000,000, the Purchase Price shall be $100,000,000 ÷ 1.020 = $98,039,215.69 1.015 = $98,522,167.49.
P241: (b) Eligible Corporate Securities:
P242: Haircut Percentage: 5.0% 3.5% (the "Corporate Haircut").

P243: Application: The Purchase Price for a Transaction in which the Purchased Securities are Eligible Corporate Securities shall be determined by dividing the Market Value of such Purchased Securities (as of the relevant Purchase Date or, in the case of Additional Purchased Securities, as of the date of transfer) by 1.050 1.035.
P244: Illustrative example: If the Market Value of Eligible Corporate Securities is $50,000,000, the Purchase Price shall be $50,000,000 ÷ 1.050 = $47,619,047.62 1.035 = $48,309,178.74.

P245: (c) The Haircut Percentages set out in this Section 4 shall apply to the initial pricing of each Transaction and to the valuation of Purchased Securities and Additional Purchased Securities for the purposes of Paragraph 4 (Margin Maintenance). For the avoidance of doubt, the Haircut Percentage applicable to a Transaction shall be determined by reference to the category of Eligible Collateral into which the relevant Purchased Securities fall at the time of the initial Transaction and shall not change during the life of that Transaction unless the Purchased Securities are substituted in accordance with Paragraph 8 and Annex II, Section 9, in which case the Haircut Percentage applicable to the Alternative Securities shall apply from the date of substitution.
P246: Section 5 — Margin Thresholds
P247: (a) Delivery Amount (Margin Deficit — payable by Seller):
P248: Margin Threshold: $250,000 (two hundred fifty thousand United States Dollars) $500,000 (five hundred thousand United States Dollars).

P249: No obligation to deliver Additional Purchased Securities or Cash Margin arises unless the Delivery Amount (calculated in the Base Currency on an aggregate net basis across all outstanding Transactions) exceeds $250,000 $500,000.
P250: (b) Return Amount (Margin Excess — payable by Buyer):
P251: Margin Threshold: $250,000 (two hundred fifty thousand United States Dollars) $500,000 (five hundred thousand United States Dollars).

P252: No obligation to return Equivalent Securities or Cash Margin arises unless the Return Amount (calculated in the Base Currency on an aggregate net basis across all outstanding Transactions) exceeds $250,000 $500,000.

P253: (c) The Margin Thresholds set forth in sub-paragraphs (a) and (b) above apply on an aggregate net basis across all outstanding Transactions. For the avoidance of doubt, the Margin Threshold is not applied on a per-Transaction basis; rather, the aggregate Delivery Amount or Return Amount across all Transactions must exceed the applicable Margin Threshold before any transfer obligation arises.
P254: Section 6 — Net Exposure Cap

P255: 6.1 The aggregate net exposure of Buyer to Seller under all Transactions outstanding at any time shall not exceed $1,500,000,000 (one billion five hundred million United States Dollars) (the "Net Exposure Cap").

P256: 6.2 For the purposes of this Section 6, "net exposure" means the aggregate Transaction Exposure of all outstanding Transactions (after application of the relevant Haircuts and after deduction of any Cash Margin held by or on behalf of Buyer), calculated in the Base Currency as of the most recent mark-to-market determination.

P257: 6.3 If at any time the net exposure would exceed the Net Exposure Cap (whether as a result of a proposed new Transaction, a decline in the Market Value of Purchased Securities, or otherwise), Buyer shall not be required to enter into any further Transaction and Seller shall, promptly upon notice from Buyer, deliver additional Eligible Collateral or cash in an amount sufficient to reduce the net exposure below the Net Exposure Cap. Failure by Seller to make such delivery within one (1) Business Day of receipt of such notice shall constitute a failure to comply with a Margin Call for the purposes of Paragraph 10(a)(ii).
P258: 6.4 The Net Exposure Cap may be amended from time to time by mutual written agreement of the parties.
P259: Section 7 — Margin Call Cut-off Time and Settlement
P260: (a) The margin call cut-off time shall be 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day.

P261: (b) If a Margin Call is given and received before 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day, the resulting transfer of Additional Purchased Securities, Equivalent Securities, or Cash Margin (as applicable) shall be effected on that same Business Day.

P262: (c) If a Margin Call is given or received at or after 10:00 a.m. London time on a Business Day, or on a day that is not a Business Day, the resulting transfer shall be effected on the next following Business Day.

P263: (d) For the purposes of this Section 7, a Margin Call shall be deemed to have been "received" at the time of actual receipt by the addressee at the notice details specified in Section 14 of this Annex II. Each party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to and acknowledge receipt of a Margin Call promptly upon receipt.
P264: Section 8 — Netting

P265: Paragraph 7(b) of the Agreement (settlement netting for obligations in the same currency falling due on the same settlement date) is elected and applicable. Accordingly, where on any Business Day amounts would otherwise be payable in the same currency and on the same settlement date by each party to the other under this Agreement, such amounts shall be netted in accordance with Paragraph 7(b) of the Agreement, and only the resulting net amount shall be payable by the party owing such amount.
P266: Section 9 — Substitution

P267: (a) Seller may, from time to time during the term of any Transaction, request the effect a substitution of Alternative Securities for all or any part of the Purchased Securities in that Transaction. Any such request notice shall be made in writing (including by electronic mail) and shall specify in reasonable detail the Purchased Securities to be replaced, the proposed Alternative Securities (including ISIN, nominal amount, issuer, coupon, maturity, and credit rating), and the proposed substitution date.

P268: (b) Any such substitution shall require the prior written consent of Buyer. Buyer may grant, withhold, condition, or delay such consent in its sole and absolute discretion and shall not be required to provide any reason for any refusal. Buyer shall use reasonable efforts to respond to any request for substitution within two (2) Business Days of receipt, but any failure to respond within such period shall not constitute consent.
P269: (b) Seller shall give Buyer not less than one (1) Business Day's prior notice of any proposed substitution. No consent of Buyer shall be required.

P270: (c) Where Buyer consents, the a substitution shall be is effected on the Business Day agreed by the parties (or, failing agreement, on the second Business Day following Buyer's consent) on the Business Day specified in Seller's notice, by simultaneous transfer of the Alternative Securities to Buyer (or to Buyer's account at the relevant settlement system) and the Purchased Securities to Seller (or to Seller's account at the relevant settlement system), through the applicable settlement system in accordance with Paragraph 6.

P271: (d) Alternative Securities must qualify as Eligible Collateral and must satisfy all of the eligibility criteria set out in Section 3 of this Annex II. The Market Value of the Alternative Securities (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) must be at least equal to the Market Value of the Purchased Securities being replaced (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage) as of the close of business on the Business Day immediately preceding the substitution date. If the Alternative Securities fall into a different category of Eligible Collateral than the Purchased Securities being replaced, the Haircut Percentage applicable to the Alternative Securities shall apply from the date of substitution.

P272: (e) Upon completion of a substitution, the Alternative Securities shall become the Purchased Securities for all purposes of the relevant Transaction, and the Confirmation for such Transaction shall be deemed to have been amended accordingly. For the avoidance of doubt, the occurrence of a substitution shall not affect the Purchase Date, the Repurchase Date, or the Pricing Rate of the relevant Transaction, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
P273: Section 10 — Cross-Default
P274: (a) For the purposes of Paragraph 10(a)(vi) of the Agreement, a "Cross-Default" shall occur with respect to a party if:

P275: (i) such party fails to make any payment or delivery when due (after giving effect to any applicable grace period) under one or more agreements or instruments relating to Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold; or

P276: (ii) such party's Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold is accelerated, or becomes capable of being accelerated, prior to its stated maturity as a result of a default (howsoever described) thereunder; or

P277: (iii) any security interest securing Specified Indebtedness in an aggregate amount exceeding the Cross-Default Threshold becomes enforceable and is enforced (including by the taking of possession or the appointment of a receiver, administrative receiver, manager, or other similar officer).

P278: (b) "Specified Indebtedness" means any obligation (whether present or future, contingent or otherwise, as principal or surety or otherwise) in respect of borrowed money. For the avoidance of doubt, Specified Indebtedness includes obligations under loan agreements, credit facilities, overdraft facilities, note purchase agreements, bond indentures, guarantees of borrowed money, and similar instruments, but excludes obligations under this Agreement and under any other agreement that is a GMRA, GMSLA, or ISDA Master Agreement between the parties.

P279: (c) "Cross-Default Threshold" means, with respect to each party, $10,000,000 (ten million United States Dollars) $50,000,000 (fifty million United States Dollars) (or its equivalent in any other currency, converted into the Base Currency at the spot rate of exchange at the relevant time).

P280: (d) For the purposes of determining whether the Cross-Default Threshold has been exceeded, all amounts of Specified Indebtedness in respect of which the relevant event has occurred shall be aggregated (regardless of whether such amounts arise under the same or different agreements or instruments).
P281: Section 11 — Act of Insolvency
P282: (a) The definition of "Act of Insolvency" shall be as set out in the 2011 ICMA GMRA, supplemented as follows.

P283: (b) Grace Period: None (zero days). An Act of Insolvency shall constitute an Event of Default immediately and automatically upon occurrence, without requirement for notice or lapse of any period of time (an "ipso facto trigger"). For the avoidance of doubt, upon the occurrence of an Act of Insolvency with respect to a party, the other party shall be entitled, without the requirement for any notice to the Defaulting Party, to designate an Early Termination Date in respect of all outstanding Transactions in accordance with Paragraph 10(b). Grace Period: Thirty (30) calendar days. An Act of Insolvency shall not constitute an Event of Default unless it has continued unremedied for a period of thirty (30) calendar days following the date on which the Non-Defaulting Party first becomes aware of, or receives written notice of, such Act of Insolvency (the "Act of Insolvency Grace Period").

P284: (c) For the avoidance of doubt, and without limiting the definition of Act of Insolvency set out in the 2011 ICMA GMRA, each of the following shall constitute an Act of Insolvency for the purposes of this Agreement:

P285: (i) the appointment of a receiver, administrator, liquidator, conservator, trustee, custodian, or similar official over a party or any material part of its assets, whether by a court of competent jurisdiction, a governmental or regulatory authority, or otherwise;

P286: (ii) the filing of any petition, application, or proceeding (whether voluntary or involuntary) seeking any such appointment or seeking any arrangement, reorganisation, composition, readjustment, liquidation, dissolution, winding-up, or similar relief under any applicable insolvency, bankruptcy, receivership, administration, or similar law;
P287: (iii) the making of a general assignment for the benefit of creditors;
P288: (iv) the admission in writing by a party of its inability to pay its debts generally as they become due;
P289: (v) the taking of any corporate or other action by a party in furtherance of any of the foregoing; or
P290: (vi) any analogous event or proceeding in any jurisdiction.
P291: Section 12 — Repricing / Mini Close-out

P292: (a) Buyer may, at its sole option, elect to reprice any Transaction having an original term or, in the case of an evergreen or rolling Transaction, a then-current term, exceeding sixty (60) calendar days. Such repricing (a "Repricing Event") may be exercised on the 90th calendar day following the Purchase Date of the relevant Transaction, or on the anniversary of any prior Repricing Date if the Transaction remains outstanding (each such date, a "Repricing Date"). If a Repricing Date falls on a day that is not a Business Day, the Repricing Date shall be the next following Business Day.

P293: (b) Buyer shall exercise a Repricing Event by delivering written notice to Seller not less than two (2) Business Days prior to the applicable Repricing Date. Such notice shall specify the Transaction to be repriced and the proposed Repricing Date.
P294: (c) Upon the occurrence of a Repricing Event:

P295: (i) the original Transaction shall terminate on the Repricing Date as if such date were the Repurchase Date, and Seller shall pay to Buyer the Repurchase Price applicable to the original Transaction as of the Repricing Date;
P296: (ii) simultaneously, the parties shall enter into a new Transaction on terms identical to the original Transaction, save that:
P297: (A) the Purchase Date of the new Transaction shall be the Repricing Date;

P298: (B) the Purchase Price of the new Transaction shall be recalculated based on the Market Value of the Purchased Securities on the Repricing Date (after application of the relevant Haircut Percentage); and

P299: (C) the Pricing Rate shall be as agreed by the parties or, failing agreement by 5:00 p.m. London time on the Business Day immediately preceding the Repricing Date, the Pricing Rate applicable to the original Transaction shall continue to apply to the new Transaction;

    paths='.//w:t|.//w:delText' if include_deleted else './/w:t'
    return ''.join((x.text or '') for x in el.xpath(paths,namespaces=ns))

def make_run(text, rpr=None, deleted=False):
    r=etree.Element(q('r'))
    if rpr is not None: r.append(deepcopy(rpr))
    t=etree.SubElement(r,q('delText' if deleted else 't'))
    if text and (text[0].isspace() or text[-1].isspace() or '  ' in text): t.set('{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space','preserve')

    for child in list(para):
        if child.tag != q('pPr'):

    clear_content(para)

from zipfile import ZipFile, ZIP_DEFLATED
from lxml import etree
from copy import deepcopy
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import os, shutil, tempfile

SRC='documents/turn-2-redline-meridian.docx'
OUT='output/turn-3-redline-gmra.docx'
W='http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main'
R='http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships'
PR='http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships'
CT='http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types'
ns={'w':W,'r':R,'pr':PR,'ct':CT}

def q(tag): return f'{{{W}}}{tag}'
def r_q(tag): return f'{{{R}}}{tag}'

def get_text(el, include_deleted=True):
    paths='.//w:t|.//w:delText' if include_deleted else './/w:t'
    return ''.join((x.text or '') for x in el.xpath(paths,namespaces=ns))

def make_run(text, rpr=None, deleted=False):
    r=etree.Element(q('r'))
    if rpr is not None: r.append(deepcopy(rpr))
    t=etree.SubElement(r,q('delText' if deleted else 't'))
    if text and (text[0].isspace() or text[-1].isspace() or '  ' in text): t.set('{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space','preserve')
    t.text=text
    return r

def first_rpr(para):
    r=para.xpath('.//w:r/w:rPr',namespaces=ns)
    return r[0] if r else None

def clear_content(para):
    for child in list(para):
        if child.tag != q('pPr'):
            para.remove(child)

def plain(para, text):
    clear_content(para)
    if text:
        para.append(make_run(text, first_rpr(para)))

def tracked_replace(para, old, new, author='Pryor, Ashworth & Gelb LLP', rid=200):
    clear_content(para)
    d=etree.SubElement(para,q('del'))
    d.set(q('id'),str(rid)); d.set(q('author'),author); d.set(q('date'),'2025-04-17T17:00:00Z')
    d.append(make_run(old, first_rpr(para), deleted=True))
    ins=etree.SubElement(para,q('ins'))
    ins.set(q('id'),str(rid+1)); ins.set(q('author'),author); ins.set(q('date'),'2025-04-17T17:00:00Z')
    ins.append(make_run(new, first_rpr(para)))

def tracked_parts(para, parts, author='Pryor, Ashworth & Gelb LLP', rid=300):
    # parts: list of ('clean'|'del'|'ins', text)
    clear_content(para)
    for kind,text in parts:
        if not text: continue
        if kind=='clean': para.append(make_run(text, first_rpr(para)))
        else:
            e=etree.SubElement(para,q('del' if kind=='del' else 'ins'))
            e.set(q('id'),str(rid)); e.set(q('author'),author); e.set(q('date'),'2025-04-17T17:00:00Z'); rid+=1
            e.append(make_run(text, first_rpr(para), deleted=(kind=='del')))

def tracked_addition(para, base, addition, author='Pryor, Ashworth & Gelb LLP', rid=500):
    clear_content(para)
    if base: para.append(make_run(base, first_rpr(para)))
    ins=etree.SubElement(para,q('ins'))
    ins.set(q('id'),str(rid)); ins.set(q('author'),author); ins.set(q('date'),'2025-04-17T17:00:00Z')
    ins.append(make_run(addition, first_rpr(para)))

def pending_insert(para, text, comment_id, author='Pryor, Ashworth & Gelb LLP', rid=700):
    clear_content(para)
    start=etree.Element(q('commentRangeStart')); start.set(q('id'),str(comment_id)); para.append(start)
    ins=etree.SubElement(para,q('ins')); ins.set(q('id'),str(rid+comment_id)); ins.set(q('author'),author); ins.set(q('date'),'2025-04-17T17:00:00Z')
    ins.append(make_run(text, first_rpr(para)))
    end=etree.Element(q('commentRangeEnd')); end.set(q('id'),str(comment_id)); para.append(end)
    rr=etree.SubElement(para,q('r'))
    rp=etree.SubElement(rr,q('rPr')); etree.SubElement(rp,q('rStyle')).set(q('val'),'CommentReference')
    cr=etree.SubElement(rr,q('commentReference')); cr.set(q('id'),str(comment_id))

def add_comment_part(files, next_rel_id):
    comments_root=etree.Element(q('comments'), nsmap={'w':W})
    comments=[]
    texts={
      1:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm acceptance or provide comments on the tax gross-up election and five Business Day cure period.',
      2:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm the G7 sovereign eligibility criteria and minimum ratings.',
      3:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm the corporate eligibility criteria, ratings and ten-year maturity limit.',
      4:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm the $1,500,000,000 Net Exposure Cap.',
      5:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm the Clearstream Banking S.A. / DTC settlement elections.',
      6:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm that bilateral settlement remains elected and BNY Meliora Trust Company, N.A. is only a contingent tri-party custodian.',
      7:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm Meridian seller notice details.',
      8:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm Voss Bank buyer notice details.',
      9:'Pending Voss Bank credit committee review — please confirm the counsel notice details for both parties.'
    }
    for i,txt in texts.items():
        c=etree.SubElement(comments_root,q('comment'))
        c.set(q('id'),str(i)); c.set(q('author'),'Rachel S. Okonkwo'); c.set(q('initials'),'RSO'); c.set(q('date'),'2025-04-17T17:00:00Z')
        p=etree.SubElement(c,q('p')); p.append(make_run(txt))

**Creating an XLSX file**

I need to create an XLSX file using openpyxl. First, I should inspect the workbook for formatting and sheet names; it shows five sheets currently. I’ll load it using openpyxl. It seems better to create a fresh, polished workbook with all the necessary sheets. I want to include an updated issues list, possibly keeping the previous one. I'll set up three sheets: Issues Tracker, Drafting Mark-Ups, and QC & Elections, plus a Summary & Key Dates. I’ll ensure to format everything correctly, particularly numeric terms.

**Detailing the QC sheet**

In the QC sheet, I need to include specific items. First, the haircuts schedule (1.75/4.25) with formulas should be checked against the schedule and instructions, noting that the buyer playbook prefers 2/5 while seller guidelines target 1.5/3.5. I’ll also specify margin thresholds: seller at 500k and buyer at 250k, confirming they were verified. Other items like net exposure caps, cross defaults, insolvency acts, and LCIA expedited caps will also be addressed. Plus, settlement notes will reference related documents, ensuring everything aligns correctly. It's crucial to verify all details!

**Organizing the QC details**

I need to include several specific items in the QC sheet. These will encompass the "Latest Buyer Position," "Latest Seller Position," "Turn 3 Position / Final Term," and details about "Movement," "Status," "Remaining Gaps," and "Negotiation Dynamics." It's also vital to outline "Next Steps / Owner" and include sources for verification. This structured approach will help ensure clarity and thoroughness, making it easier to track progress and responsibilities throughout the negotiation process. Keeping everything organized is key!
